entries.methodology: 60-day IL freezes a player's 40-man roster slot. 15-day IL is the standard major-injury duration. The site surfaces every IL stint over the trailing 12 months; the Health profile aggregates the count and total IL days.

entries.definition: 20-80 scouting grade for a pitcher's fastball - velocity, movement, shape, and command of the pitch.
entries.methodology: Most pitchers' headline tool. 60+ is plus (mid-90s + ride or sink); 70+ is plus-plus (upper-90s + carry). The grade folds together velo, vertical/horizontal break, and command of the pitch; pure velo without shape rarely earns above 55.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the pitcher's slider (or sweeper variant) - sharpness, depth, tunneling with the fastball.
entries.methodology: Sliders sit ~5-10 mph below the FB; sweepers add ~15-18 inches of horizontal break. Both ride the 'sl' slot in our data because their roles overlap. 60+ is a true out-pitch slider; 50 is average MLB shape.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the curveball - depth, shape, and command of the slowest breaking pitch.
entries.methodology: Distinct from a slider by velocity (8-12 mph slower than the FB vs. 5-10) and by primarily vertical break. Spike/knuckle/standard grips all map to 'cb' in our data. 60+ curveballs typically pair with a deep FB slot (over-the-top arm action).

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the changeup (or splitter) - velo separation, arm-action deception, and command.
entries.methodology: Changeups sit 8-12 mph below the FB with sink/fade. Splitters sit 8-12 mph below with hard tumble - different grip, same role in the arsenal. Both ride the 'ch' slot. 60+ changeups define a starter's profile vs. lefties.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the ability to locate pitches WITHIN the strike zone (not just throw strikes).
entries.methodology: Control = ability to throw strikes; Command = ability to throw the right strike. Plus command (60+) means consistently spotting the FB on the corner, burying the breaker below the zone, etc. Most prospects sit 45-50; a 60 command grade dramatically lifts the ceiling.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for the cutter - a hybrid between FB and slider with late horizontal break, ~3-5 mph below the FB.
entries.methodology: FG and Pipeline don't always grade the cutter as a distinct slot; Just Baseball does. We carry 'ct' as a canonical key so JB-graded cutters flow into consensus when published. The pitch's role is FB-like (in-zone, two-strike strike-out option) but with arm-side cut.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for a hitter's swing decisions and pitch recognition - chase / contact rate / zone awareness.
entries.methodology: A separate skill from the hit tool (bat-to-ball). 60+ pitch selection means low chase, high z-contact, willingness to take walks. FG publishes this as a standalone grade; Just Baseball calls it 'Plate Disc.'. Feeds the offensive composite alongside Hit / Game Power.

entries.definition: 20-80 grade for barrel control - the ability to manipulate the bat in-zone, foul off tough pitches, square balls up.
entries.methodology: Distinct from the broader hit tool. Bat control speaks to swing path quality, bat-head awareness, and 2-strike adjustability - the difference between a plus hitter who barrels everything (60+) and one who hits .280 but chases the barrel (50).

entries.definition: MLB's December draft of minor leaguers left unprotected by their org. Selecting team must keep the player on its MLB 26-man all season or offer them back.
entries.methodology: Held during the Winter Meetings (early December). Any player signed at 18+ with 4 years of pro service, or at 19+ with 5 years, must be added to the 40-man roster by the Nov 20 protection deadline or risk Rule 5 selection. Picks cost $100K. Returning a Rule 5 pick costs the selecting team $50K.

entries.definition: The annual July amateur player draft - 20 rounds, picks from US/Canada/Puerto Rico HS and college. Distinct from the Rule 5 (Dec) draft.
entries.methodology: Each team has a bonus pool sized to their pick slot values; spending under pool saves nothing, spending over by >5% triggers picks-forfeiture penalties. International players (DSL/Latin America) don't go through Rule 4 - they sign as IFAs.

entries.definition: The 40 players a team can call up to MLB without exposing to other clubs. Drives Rule 5 protection deadlines.
entries.methodology: Includes the active 26-man + players on the 10/15-day IL + minor leaguers added to protect from Rule 5. The 60-day IL adds an EXTRA slot temporarily. Teams crunch to fit 40 every November; DFAs and trades shake players loose.

entries.definition: Each 40-man player has 3 (sometimes 4) option years allowing free MLB↔AAA shuttle. After they're used, the player must clear waivers to be sent down.
entries.methodology: An 'option' is burned the first time a player is sent to the minors in a season AND spends 20+ days there. Burning an option each of three seasons exhausts them. Out-of-options players are higher-stakes 40-man slots - they can't be sent down freely.

entries.definition: MLB days accrued on the active roster or IL. 172 days = 1 'year' of service. 3 yrs → arbitration; 6 yrs → free agency.
entries.methodology: The single biggest factor in a player's career economics. Teams routinely 'manipulate' service time by holding rookies in AAA for 2-3 weeks to preserve a year of team control. 'Super Two' is the additional ~22% of 2-yr players who reach arbitration a year early.

entries.definition: Salary process for players with 3-6 yrs of MLB service. Player + team file binding numbers; an arbitrator picks one if they don't settle.
entries.methodology: Arbitration cases are heard in February. The arbitrator picks ONE side's number - no splitting. Most cases settle before the hearing. Arb-year salaries scale up year over year (Yr1 ~$1M, Yr3 ~$8M for stars). Super Twos get a 4th arb year.

entries.definition: Service-time window from 0 to ~3 yrs MLB time. Player is paid at or near the league minimum with no salary leverage.
entries.methodology: Pre-arb is the most team-friendly part of a player's career - most graduates spend their first 2-3 MLB years here. Salaries are unilaterally set by the club (subject to league minimum, ~$760k in 2024). The new CBA introduced a Pre-Arb Bonus Pool that retroactively rewards top performers but doesn't change the unilateral-pay structure. Once the player crosses 3.000 of MLB service (or qualifies as Super Two), they enter arbitration.

entries.definition: Players in the top 22% of 2-3 service-year players get a 4th arbitration year. Costs the team an extra arb cycle.
entries.methodology: After each season, MLB identifies players with between 2.000 and 3.000 of service time. The top 22% by service days qualify as Super Two and become arb-eligible a year early. Teams aggressively manage call-ups to keep top prospects below the Super Two cutoff - usually requires keeping the player on the active roster for fewer than ~125 days in his first MLB season.

entries.definition: Strategic delay of a top prospect's MLB debut to gain an extra year of team control. Less common post-2022 CBA but not eliminated.
entries.methodology: If a club holds a prospect in AAA for the first ~3 weeks of the regular season, the player won't accumulate 172 days of MLB service that year - pushing free agency back by a year. The 2022 CBA introduced PPI (Prospect Promotion Incentive) draft picks for clubs that promote top prospects on Opening Day AND those players finish top-2 in ROY voting or top-5 in MVP/Cy Young - partially aligning incentives. Famous examples: Kris Bryant (2015 grievance lost), Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (2019 demotion).

entries.definition: Players with 6+ years of MLB service may sign with any club once the World Series ends; the first five days are an exclusive-negotiation window with the incumbent club and the qualifying-offer period.
entries.methodology: Major-league free agency requires 6.000 of service time. The 5-day window after the World Series is exclusive negotiating period with the prior team; after that, the player is open to all 30 clubs. Minor-league free agency is separate - minor-leaguers become 6-year MiLB FAs after their 6th professional season unless on a 40-man roster. Spotrac, MLB Trade Rumors, and Baseball-Reference all track FA classes by year.

entries.definition: One-year contract a club may offer its departing free agent at the mean of MLB's top-125 salaries (~$21M in 2024). If the player declines and signs elsewhere, the SIGNING club forfeits draft-pick compensation and the former club gains a comp pick - the offer itself costs the old club nothing beyond the one-year salary risk.
entries.methodology: Teams can extend a QO to free agents who spent the entire prior season with the team and haven't received one before. If the player declines (almost always) and signs elsewhere, the signing team forfeits draft picks; the losing team gets a compensation pick. The QO value is calculated annually as the simple average of the top 125 player salaries. Mid-season trade acquisitions are NOT QO-eligible (a key trade-deadline tax).

entries.definition: Extra draft picks awarded for QO-declined free agents, Prospect Promotion Incentive (PPI), and revenue-sharing balance.
entries.methodology: Two main sources: (1) QO comp - teams losing a QO'd FA get a pick after either round 1 (small-market teams) or after round 4 (mid/large markets, depending on luxury-tax status). The signing team forfeits a pick to balance. (2) PPI - clubs that promote a top prospect on Opening Day and the player wins ROY (or top-2) earn a pick after round 1. The Competitive Balance Lottery also awards 10-12 picks (Round A + Round B) to lower-revenue clubs.

entries.definition: Post-DFA path - player clears waivers and is sent off the 40-man roster down to AAA. Player can refuse if they have 3+ MLB service yrs.
entries.methodology: After a DFA, the team has 7 days. If the player clears waivers (no other club claims them), they can be outrighted to AAA. The player loses 40-man protection but keeps minor-league assignment rights. Players with 3+ MLB service years OR a prior outright in their career can REFUSE the outright and elect free agency. Each outright stays on the player's record permanently.

entries.definition: Removal from the 40-man roster. Team has 7 days to trade, waive, or release the player. A common 40-man crunch mechanism.
entries.methodology: A DFA freezes the player off the active roster and starts the 7-day clock. Outcomes: outright to AAA (player can refuse if they have 3+ MLB service yrs), waiver claim (any other team grabs them), trade, or release. Most DFA'd players clear waivers and accept the outright.

entries.definition: First MLB appearance. Per the v21 debut rule, mlbDebutDate being set moves a prospect to the Debuted tab.
entries.methodology: We mark MLB debuts with a ★ chip on the transaction-history table. Pre-debut, a prospect's value is theoretical; post-debut, the FV starts converting to (or away from) real MLB performance. Debut removes a player from the active prospect lists and surfaces them on the Debuted tab.

entries.definition: Lump-sum payment at signing for amateur players. Draftees pull from the team's draft pool; IFAs from the IFA pool.
entries.methodology: Draft slot values are published each year by MLB. Teams can spend up to 5% over pool with progressive tax penalties; >5% costs future first-round picks. IFA bonuses are capped at the assigned pool size (~$5.95M base + competitive-balance bonuses) - no overage allowed since 2017.

entries.definition: Three IL durations: 10-day (position players), 15-day (the minimum for pitchers and two-way players, post-2022), and 60-day, which also frees the player's 40-man roster spot.
entries.methodology: A team can transfer between IL types - a 15-day IL stint can convert to 60-day when the player misses more time. The 60-day IL removes the player from the 40-man count (extra roster flexibility). Concussion IL is a separate 7-day version.

entries.definition: Official MLB designation: 20+ MLB innings pitched AND 20+ MLB games started as a position player or DH with at least 3 plate appearances in each. Qualifying exempts the player from the pitcher-usage rules that bar position players from pitching in competitive games.
entries.methodology: Ohtani is the canonical example. The site detects two-way profiles when a prospect has both hitter (hit/game_pwr/...) AND pitcher (fb/sl/...) canonical tool grades - both Tools cards then render. Reggie Crawford and a handful of recent draftees fit the pattern.

entries.definition: Scouting grades come in pairs: present grade (what they show today) and future grade (projected peak). FG ships them as 'Hit 30/55' = present 30, future 55.
entries.methodology: We always store the FUTURE grade as the canonical tool number (the projection is the actionable signal). Present grades ride alongside in _extras['present'] for sources that publish both. The gap between present and future encodes risk / development runway.

entries.definition: Rookie-level stateside ball played at team training complexes (Arizona or Florida). Mostly recent draftees + DSL graduates.
entries.methodology: Two leagues: ACL (Arizona Complex League, ex-AZL) and FCL (Florida Complex League, ex-GCL). Games at team backfields, no fans. Players are 17-20. The 2021 MiLB reorg consolidated the older rookie-level leagues into these two.

entries.definition: Green ▲ = consensus FV rose since the last update; red ▼ = fell. Magnitude is the FV-delta.
entries.methodology: Stock is the consensus-FV delta since the most recent prior update - a player with only one update reads as 'flat'. Drives the 'Up' / 'Down' filter on the Active list; movements ≥ 1.5 grade-points show in the row's meta line.

Rarity ramp anchored at FV 40 (baseline) with HOLO above CHROME (chrome is static silver; holo carries the rainbow shift, so the rainbow tier reads as rarer). Five rarity bands above the baseline, mirroring the Topps Chrome / refractor aesthetic:\

entries.definition: 4-branch farm grade (v40 - VALUE-TRACKING). Composite = Value 65% (aggregate risk-adjusted surplus) · MLB Production 18% (raw graduate WAR) · Development 9% · Acquisition 8%.
entries.methodology:
Grade tree v40 - recalibrated to PRIMARILY track aggregate value. The grade was previously a per-prospect tool-development index (Development 50%, with the surplus leaf normalized to a PER-PROSPECT figure), which decoupled it from a system's total value: a farm could be 3rd in total surplus yet grade 15th, below a 25th-in-surplus farm. v40 fixes that.

Weights: Value 65% / MLB Production 18% / Development 9% / Acquisition 8%. (1) The Value branch is driven by AGGREGATE risk-adjusted controlled surplus - the total $ value of the org's active prospect pool from the recalibrated value_framework, which already prices elite ceiling non-linearly, so it captures top-end-vs-depth on its own (no opaque top-heavy weighting).

(2) MLB Production grades on RAW realized graduate WAR (WAR/yr + Top-3 cumulative WAR + boom/−bust/top-grads/conviction/HOF-track); the WAG talent-translation leaf is DROPPED from the rollup (raw MLB output over translation-vs-grade). (3) Development (per-tool DvM+) and Acquisition stay as secondary controllable-skill / process signals.

Validation against realized output: grade-rank now correlates +0.85 with total-surplus rank (was +0.38); every remaining deviation is production-explained - orgs grading above their surplus rank lead the league in realized graduate WAR (e.g. ATL #1), orgs below are near-last.

Letter scale: A+ #1, A top 7%, F bottom ~3%. Every leaf z-scored across the 30 orgs; sparse leaves get ' - '. A continuous TIEBREAKER score differentiates same-grade farms - see farm_tiebreaker.
entries.formula:
farm_score = 0.65·Value + 0.18·MLB_Production + 0.09·Development + 0.08·Acquisition
  Value          = wmean(Aggregate_active_surplus[0.68], Org_$DvM+, Grad_contract_surplus, WAR_per_$M, Draft_pool_eff, IFA_ROI)
  MLB_Production  = mean(Hitter_WAR/yr+Top3, Pitcher_WAR/yr+Top3, Boom%, -Bust%, Top3_WAR/yr, Conviction, HOF_track)
  Development     = mean(Hitter_Tools_DvM+, Pitcher_Tools_DvM+, Health_Mgmt, Statcast_Quality)
  Acquisition     = mean(Draft, IFA-ROI, Trade, Waiver)
  tiebreaker = 100 + 10·(0.40·z(total_surplus) + 0.25·z(6yDvM+) + 0.35·z(raw_graduate_WAR))
entries.example: A system graded A- with branches Value A, MLB Production B+, Development B, Acquisition B- is winning on aggregate risk-adjusted surplus (the 65% branch) while its trade ledger lags; the Tendencies tab shows which acquisition channels drive the B-.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Continuous score differentiating farms that share a letter grade. 100 = league mean, +10 = 1σ.
entries.methodology: Coarse letter grades collapse real value gaps - two clearly different farms can share a grade. The tiebreaker is a continuous, league-normalized blend of the three value dimensions, shown under each farm's letter so same-grade systems are ordered and distinguishable: 0.40·total active surplus + 0.25·6yDvM+ + 0.35·raw graduate WAR (z-scored across the 30 orgs, anchored 100 + 10·z). Total surplus and 6yDvM+ are the dollar and indexed views of one controlled-value concept, so they share weight rather than double-count; raw graduate WAR adds the REALIZED-output axis (actual MLB WAR produced by the org's graduates - not WAG) that the paper-value measures can't see. Carries a component breakdown and a finer continuous 1-30 rank alongside the letter grade.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Outcome quality of how this org acquires prospects across all 4 channels: Draft, IFA, Trade, Waiver.
entries.methodology:
Acquisition Strategy branch of the farm grade tree (15% of farm_score in v5; was 20% in v4; merged what were Acquisitions + Transactions in v2). Four sub-leaves, equal weight: (a) Draft Performance - 50/50 blend of pick-slot-adjusted WAR (career WAR vs. historical expectation at that pick slot) + Draft Ceiling Hits % (recent drafted actives at FV ≥ 60 within 3yr of draft).

(b) IFA Performance - 3-input composite of WAG + WAR-per-year + Cumulative WAR across IFA-method graduates. (c) Trade Acumen - net FV gained vs lost at trade dates + Trade WAR Delta (career WAR of acquired grads − career WAR of traded-away grads).

(d) Waiver Claims - net FV from non-trade cross-org events + Waiver Hit Rate (% of claims who reached MLB). Each leaf z-scored across orgs; sparse leaves get ' - '.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-tool dev pace of the org's prospects vs the league. SOLO TOP-WEIGHTED branch (v5: 40%) - the single biggest controllable skill the org has direct hands on.
entries.methodology: Development branch of the farm grade tree. Two sub-grades, equal weight: (a) Hitter Tools DvM+ - mean of HitDvM+ / PowerDvM+ / SpeedDvM+ / FieldDvM+ / ArmDvM+ / PitchSelDvM+ / BatCtrlDvM+ for this org's actives, (b) Pitcher Tools DvM+ - mean of FB / SL / CB / CH / Cmd / CtDvM+. Both 100-anchored (100 = league mean dev pace, +10 = 1σ). Measures pure tool growth in-org, independent of raw FV - a 40-grade hit tool that grew to 55 over 2 cycles signals development skill regardless of where the prospect started.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The org's aggregate risk-adjusted controlled value. PRIMARY grade branch (v40 - 65% of the composite). Dominated by total active-pool surplus.
entries.methodology:
Value branch of the farm grade tree (the Financial branch reframed; 65% of farm_score in v40, up from 18%). The largest grade input: a farm's grade should principally reflect the total risk-adjusted value of its active prospect pool.

The dominant leaf (0.68) is AGGREGATE active surplus: the summed FV-implied, risk-adjusted, present-valued controlled surplus across the org's active prospects (recalibrated value_framework), which prices elite ceiling non-linearly so the total captures top-end-vs-depth without a separate premium. Secondary leaves add texture: Org $DvM+ (do these prospects appreciate vs FV-tier peers), grad-contract surplus, WAR per $M, draft-pool efficiency, IFA ROI.

The prior spec scored the surplus leaf PER PROSPECT (normalizing aggregate away), which is why a high-total-value farm couldn't grade up; v40 scores it on the total. 100-anchored (+10 = 1σ).
entries.formula: Value_score = wmean( aggregate_active_surplus[0.68], org_$DvM+[0.10], grad_contract_surplus[0.10], war_per_$M[0.04], draft_pool_eff[0.04], IFA_ROI[0.04] )
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Whether the org produces MLB players, especially top-end ones. v7 leaves (6): hitter + pitcher WAR/yr + Top-3, boom rate, BUST rate, top-3 grad WAR/yr, Conviction.
entries.methodology:
MLB Production branch (25% of farm_score in v7; was 30% in v6 - Development absorbed the freed weight). Six sub-grades, equal weight: (a) Hitter MLB Production - z-blend of Hitter WAR-per-year + Top-3 Hitter Career WAR (v7 dropped WAG - WAG now lives in Acquisition Strategy as the talent-translation signal).

(b) Pitcher MLB Production - same 2-input composite for pitchers. (c) Boom Rate - share of settled grads with career WAR ≥ +5 (min 5 settled). (d) BUST Rate - NEW v7 - share of settled grads with career WAR ≤ +1, entered as a NEGATIVE-direction input so bust-heavy orgs get penalized.

(e) Top-3 Grad WAR/yr - mean WAR/yr of the org's top-3 grads by rate (min 3 qualifying). (f) Conviction - binary flag: 1 if any grad has WAR/yr ≥ 4.0 in trailing 6yr OR career WAR ≥ 12 ever, else 0.

Conviction additionally drives the farm-score cap: conviction=0 orgs clamp at the 75th-percentile farm_score regardless of branch grades.
entries.formula:
Production_score = mean of z-anchored (Hitter_WAR/yr+Top3, Pitcher_WAR/yr+Top3, boom_pct, -bust_pct, top3_WAR_per_yr, conviction)
Conviction cap: if conviction = 0 and farm_score > p75 → farm_score = p75
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of an org's settled MLB graduates with career WAR ≥ +5 (true 'boom' outcomes).
entries.methodology: Boom Rate leaf inside MLB Production. For each graduate the org produced, classify as boom / settled / bust once the player meets a sample floor (800 PA / 200 IP / ≥2 MLB seasons). Boom = career WAR ≥ +5 (well above replacement, regular-to-star outcome). Boom Rate = boom_count / settled_count. Min 5 settled grads or the leaf returns ' - '. Pairs with `mlb_production_bust_pct` (negative-direction leaf) to give the composite both 'reward for hits' and 'penalty for misses'.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of an org's settled MLB graduates with career WAR ≤ +1 (bust outcomes). NEGATIVE-direction input to MLB Production.
entries.methodology: Bust Rate leaf inside MLB Production (v7 - new). Mirror of Boom Rate using the same sample floor (800 PA / 200 IP / ≥2 MLB seasons): bust = career WAR ≤ +1 (replacement-or-below outcome). Bust Rate = bust_count / settled_count. Min 5 settled grads or the leaf returns ' - '. Enters the MLB Production composite as a NEGATIVE input: higher bust % pulls the parent grade DOWN, opposite to Boom Rate.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Mean WAR/yr across the org's top-3 graduates by rate. Captures peak star-tier production without depth dilution.
entries.methodology: Top-3 Grad WAR/yr leaf inside MLB Production v4. For each graduate meeting the boom-bust sample floor (≥800 PA / ≥200 IP / ≥2 MLB seasons), compute WAR/yr (career WAR / MLB seasons). Sort desc, take mean of top 3. Min 3 qualifying grads or the leaf returns ' - '. An org producing one Skenes + two solid regulars (e.g. 5.0 + 2.5 + 2.0 / 3 = 3.17) scores far above one producing 10 league-average grads (1.0 + 1.0 + 1.0 = 1.0). Pairs with `mlb_production_top_grads_pitcher_only` for position-group breakdowns.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Binary 0/1 flag: org has produced at least one star-tier grad (WAR/yr ≥ 4.0 last 6yr OR career WAR ≥ 12 ever). Drives the farm-score cap.
entries.methodology: Conviction leaf inside MLB Production v4. Fires (=1) if at least one graduate satisfies EITHER (a) WAR/yr ≥ 4.0 (All-Star tier) with last MLB year within the trailing 6 years, OR (b) career WAR ≥ 12 ever (high-end Hall-of-Very-Good output). Otherwise =0. PIT (Skenes) → 1; KCR (Witt Jr.) → 1; orgs without a recent star → 0. Beyond contributing as a leaf input, Conviction drives a post-process **farm-score cap**: conviction=0 orgs whose composite would exceed the 75th-percentile farm_score get clamped to that p75 value. This prevents depth-only orgs from grading elite without a star ceiling - they can still be A-tier in depth / acquisitions / development, but not the very top.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Trailing-3yr-window WAR per $M (and v32.0 - FV per $M) of draft-pool spend.
entries.methodology:
Draft Pool Efficiency leaf inside Financial. Two signals on the same denominator (pool $ spent in T-5..T-2):
• **war_per_m_pool** - sum of career WAR for grads drafted in the window divided by pool $M. Lagging but realized: WAR only accrues after the prospect debuts. Gated at ≥3 grads.
• **fv_per_m_pool** (v32.0) - sum of current FV across drafted-actives in the same window divided by pool $M. Fast-cycle companion: doesn't wait the typical 5yr for WAR maturation, so the signal is responsive within ~2yr of draft.
Denominator comes from MLB-published per-team draft pools (from `mlb_draft_pools` org-summary data). Together these capture both slot-money discipline + late-round hits (WAR side) AND scouting/dev acceleration (FV side).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Trailing-6yr-window WAR per $M of IFA bonus spend. Captures whether the org's international signings translated to MLB production.
entries.methodology: IFA ROI leaf inside Financial v6. Numerator: sum of career WAR for IFA-method grads signed in (T-9)…(T-3) - 6-year rolling window (bumped from 5yr in v6 to align with the 6y DvM+ horizon). IFA prospects need more development time than draft picks, so the window starts ~9 years out and ends ~3 years out. Denominator: sum of org's total IFA bonus spending over those same signing years (from the per-year IFA spend table). Output: WAR/$M. Gated at ≥2 contributing grads with signed_year + bonus on file. Cubans / Asian-pro signings + bonus-pool-busting splash signings show up here as high-spend low-ROI; orgs that develop deep $200K-$500K signings (e.g. Cleveland's Latin America operation) show high ROI.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Capital-efficiency index for farm systems. 100 = league mean, +10 = 1σ.
entries.methodology: Org-level composite of WAR/$M (existing Financial ROI) and Grad-Contract Surplus (current AAV − amortized bonus per year). Each input z-scored across the 30 orgs and anchored at 100. Mirrors the wRC+/OPS+ shape so the reader can compare it against DvM+ + ToolDvM+ on the same dial. Powers the Financial branch of the farm grade tree. NOTE: distinct from Sur+, which is the per-prospect $M surplus-value projection.
entries.formula: OrgSur+ = 100 + 10 · avg(z(WAR/$M), z(grad contract surplus))
entries.example: An org producing 0.8 graduate WAR per $M of bonus spend (one stddev above the mean) and league-average graduate contract surplus posts OrgSur+ around 105: capital-efficient on the draft side, ordinary on the development-to-contract side.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: % of recent (≤3yr) drafted actives at FV ≥ 60. Captures whether the org drafted high-ceiling talent, not just talent that beat the slot.
entries.methodology: One of the two sub-inputs feeding the Draft Performance leaf (the other is pick-slot-adjusted WAR). For each org, count drafted actives whose current consensus FV ≥ 60 AND whose draft year is within the trailing 3 years. Divide by the count of all drafted actives in that 3-year window. Sparse-data gate: <3 drafted actives → ' - '. The ceiling-hits metric complements pick-slot-adjusted WAR (which is retrospective and grad-only) by capturing whether the most recent draft classes already show top-prospect upside.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Career WAR of acquired-in-trade graduates minus career WAR of traded-away graduates. Captures retrospective trade value.
entries.methodology: One of the two sub-inputs feeding the Trade Acumen leaf (the other is net FV at trade date). Per org, sum the career WAR of every graduate the org acquired via trade, then subtract the sum of career WAR of every graduate the org traded away. Positive = org came out ahead on the actual MLB production of traded-prospect-now-graduate. Useful complement to net FV because the league's FV consensus at the trade date can lag or lead actual development.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: % of waiver-claimed prospects who reached MLB. Sparse-data signal - orgs with <3 claims grade ' - '.
entries.methodology: One of the two sub-inputs feeding the Waiver Claims leaf (the other is net FV from non-trade cross-org events). Per org, count claimed-into-org prospects whose career_war field is populated (= reached MLB at any point), divide by total claimed-into-org count. Captures whether the org's waiver-claim decisions actually translated to MLB rosters, separate from the FV-at-claim signal.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Cross-org player swap. The Transactions branch of the farm grade tree rolls up net trade FV per org.
entries.methodology: Every trade involving a tracked prospect generates two fv_events on the org timeline: a 'trade out' on the sending org and a 'trade in' on the receiving org, both stamped with the prospect's consensus FV at the trade date. Per-org net = sum(fv_in) − sum(fv_out). Higher net = better trade acumen (the org captured more talent than it gave up at the FV the league assigned on the trade date). A fair trade by retrospective WAR can still register asymmetrically here because trade-date FV may have lagged or led actual development.

entries.definition: Non-trade cross-org acquisition. Counted in the Transactions branch alongside trades.
entries.methodology: Includes waiver claims, Rule 5 selections + returns, contract purchases, and free-agent signings. Each event generates a non-trade fv_event tagged with the prospect's most-recent consensus FV (vs trades which use FV at the trade date - waivers happen on too short a timeline for an explicit FV-at-date lookup to be worth the cost). The Acquisition Strategy branch's Waiver Claims sub-grade sums these per org as a net FV: claimed-in minus released-out.

entries.definition: Per-org mean WAG across recent graduates. Positive = farm beats projections; negative = underperforms.
entries.methodology: For each graduate with both a final FV and career WAR on file, we compute WAG = actual_career_WAR − FV-implied expected_WAR (via the hardcoded FV→WAR primer table). Per-org grade = mean of WAG values. Orgs with fewer than 3 qualifying graduates grade as ' - ' rather than picking up an unfair letter off one data point.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: WAR-per-million-dollars-spent across the org's graduates. Pure capital efficiency.
entries.methodology: Aggregates total career WAR yielded by graduates against total signing-bonus dollars paid (draft + IFA). Higher = better bargain capture. Lagging indicator - a recent draft class hasn't converted yet. Orgs with fewer than 3 grads with both bonus AND career-WAR data on file grade as ' - '.
entries.formula: ROI = total_career_WAR / (total_bonus_USD / 1,000,000)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Top-10 mean of composite_overall (the org's Tool composite) across active prospects. Raw scouting quality, orthogonal to FV consensus.
entries.methodology: We rank an org's actives by composite_overall (the 20-80 power-mean of their per-tool grades that drives Tool / O-Tool / D-Tool) and take the top 10. Top-10 (not all-active mean) so a top-heavy farm with raw-tools stars isn't dragged down by un-graded depth. A '60 raw power' system grades higher than a '50 across the board' system, even if their FV consensus is the same.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: IFA % × multi-year diversity. Rewards orgs with broad, steady international scouting.
entries.methodology: Combines magnitude (IFA share of actives) and diversity (number of distinct IFA signing years represented). Score = 0.7 × ifa_pct + 0.3 × (year_span / 10, capped at 1.0). Penalizes draft-only feast/famine; rewards a steady DR/VZ/Cuba pipeline.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of prospects flagged 'very young for level' minus 'very old for level'. Long runway vs peaking now.
entries.methodology: Per-org (very_young_count − very_old_count) / total_actives. Positive = many under-age prospects (long development horizon); negative = old-for-level system that's peaking now. Uses the same per-prospect age_vs_level tiers the row chip uses.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Combined post-TJ % and trailing 12-month IL-days mean. INVERSE - lower burden = better letter grade.
entries.methodology: Per-org health_burden displays the legacy 100 × post_tj_pct + il_days_mean composite for back-compat, but the v31.6 Health Mgmt LEAF GRADE no longer includes post-TJ (post-surgery grace period often produces above-avg outcomes, and TJ for hitters isn't a real signal). Current Health Mgmt leaf scoring = IL% current + avg 12-month IL days, both inverted. Post-TJ pitcher counts still ship as informational context on the leaf but no longer affect the grade.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Share of an org's tracked actives currently on the injured list (any type). Snapshot, not trailing window.
entries.methodology: Per-org il_pct_current = il_current_count / active_count, computed at export time from the il_status table (the same source the per-player IL chip uses). Distinct from Health Burden, which weights 12-month IL DAYS - this metric just counts WHO IS DOWN RIGHT NOW. Surfaced on the Roster Snapshot tile and highlighted red when ≥10% of the org is currently sidelined.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Year-grouped view of MLB-signed overseas free agents (NPB / KBO / CPBL / etc.), with per-class rollups for total bonus, mean WAG, and mean WAR/yr.
entries.methodology: Lives on the Overseas page → Signed sub-tab. Every signed prospect is grouped by `posting_year` (posted_date.year, falling back to signed_date.year). Each year-section shows class totals (count, $ bonuses paid) plus mean WAG and mean WAR/yr across signees that have accumulated ≥1 full-season MLB sample. Both performance numbers are sourced via the prospect's `milb_key` joining to the graduate's career_war + boom-label payload - same numbers the boom-bust pill and farm grade tree consume.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Extra draft slots awarded to small-revenue clubs under the 2022 CBA. Round 1A (6 picks) lands after round 1; Round 1B (6 picks) lands after round 2.
entries.methodology: Eligible clubs are the 6 smallest-revenue + 6 smallest-market teams. Round 1A picks are slotted after the regular first round (pick 31-36); Round 1B picks land after the regular second round. They're TRADEABLE - comp picks are the only draft slots a team may swap. Tankathon's projection assigns these by current eligibility; the lottery view surfaces them at the bottom with a 1A / 1B label.

entries.definition: Post-All-Star-break snapshots subtract 0.25 years from the ETA - scaled by the org's historical H1/H2 promotion tendency (H2-heavy orgs get a stronger pull-in).
entries.methodology:
MLB's All-Star break (anchored to July 15 as a stable midpoint) cleaves the season into pre-break (H1) and post-break (H2) halves. By H2, a AAA prospect has already burned roughly half their AAA year, so the level-baseline travel time to MLB should shrink correspondingly.

The baseline adjustment subtracts 0.25 years when the snapshot is post-break. ORG TENDENCY then scales: each org's last 3 years of promotions are bucketed H1/H2. Orgs with h2_rate ≥ 60% (TBR / OAK-types that bank Sept call-ups) get a stronger ×1.4 pull-in; orgs with h1_rate ≥ 70% (front-loaded promoters) get a softer ×0.6 since they've already done most of their calling.

H2-heavy orgs during pre-break add a small +0.10 push-back (their prospect is even LESS likely to debut before the break). Offseason snapshots (Nov-Feb) and balanced orgs (40-60 split) get no adjustment.

Surfaced via a 'Snapshot: post-All-Star break' eyebrow + an 'Org promotes X% H1 / Y% H2' line on the ETA panel. Implemented in eta.py · see `season_phase`, `HALF_SEASON_ADJ`, `_org_promotion_phase_weight`.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-level + per-side age threshold that gates excessively-old prospects out of the Risers / Rebounders / Fallers buckets. Anchored on the prospect-aspirational level baseline (A=21, A+=22, AA=23, AAA=24, MLB=26).
entries.methodology:
Hitters get disqualified when their age is ≥ +2.0 years above the level baseline; pitchers get a 1-year grace (≥ +3.0) since later debuts are common. Anchored on aspirational baselines NOT empirical level means - the empirical AAA pool is dragged up by the same journeymen we're trying to filter, so anchoring on the empirical median defeats the purpose.

Examples (AAA, baseline 24): a 26.0+ hitter is cut; a 27.0+ pitcher is cut. The cap fires inside `_classify_movement` in spotlights.py BEFORE bucket classification - capped prospects return bucket='none' and never reach the Risers / Fallers / Rebounders lists.

Players at rookie levels (DSL/CPX/ROK) and players with missing age/level pass through (no cap fires). The cap is SPECIFIC to the spotlights section - it does not affect the active prospect list, farm rosters, leaderboards, or any other view.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How hard a hitter strikes the ball, in mph off the bat. Higher = louder contact and more damage on balls in play.
entries.methodology: Average exit velocity is the mean batted-ball speed measured at contact. It is the most stable batted-ball signal at small samples - it stabilizes in ~40 batted balls, far faster than results stats - so it reads a prospect's raw contact quality before the surface stats settle. Pairs with launch angle to produce barrels. League-average MLB EV is ~89 mph; 92+ is plus, 95+ is elite (Stanton/Judge tier).
entries.example: A prospect averaging 92.5 mph EV sits roughly one standard deviation above the MLB mean - a plus raw-power signal even on a modest slash line.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): the speed of the ball off the bat.

entries.definition: Share of batted balls hit in the EV + launch-angle window that historically produces ≥ .500 AVG and ≥ 1.500 SLG. The most predictive single contact-damage signal.
entries.methodology: A 'barrel' is a batted ball whose exit-velocity / launch-angle combination has historically yielded at least a .500 batting average and 1.500 slugging. Barrel% = barrels ÷ batted balls. It isolates the loud, optimally-angled contact that drives extra-base power, filtering out both weak contact and hard-but-mishit balls. League average is ~8%; 12%+ is plus, 16%+ is elite.
entries.formula:
Barrel% = barrels / batted_balls × 100
barrel = (EV, launch angle) in the ≥.500 AVG / ≥1.500 SLG zone
entries.example: A hitter at 14% Barrel% on a full-season MiLB sample profiles as plus game power even if his HR total looks ordinary for the park.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): a barrel is a batted ball whose exit velocity and launch angle historically produce elite results.

entries.definition: Share of batted balls hit ≥ 95 mph. A volume measure of quality contact - broader than Barrel% (no angle requirement).
entries.methodology: Hard-Hit% = batted balls at or above 95 mph ÷ all batted balls. It captures how often a hitter makes authoritative contact regardless of angle, so it complements Barrel% (which adds the angle requirement). League average is ~40%; 45%+ is plus. High Hard-Hit% with low Barrel% flags a hitter who needs a launch-angle adjustment to convert raw power into game power.
entries.formula: Hard-Hit% = batted_balls ≥ 95 mph / batted_balls × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): share of batted balls hit 95+ mph.

entries.definition: Share of pitches OUTSIDE the strike zone that a hitter swings at. Lower = better plate discipline.
entries.methodology: Chase% (a.k.a. O-Swing%) = swings on out-of-zone pitches ÷ out-of-zone pitches seen. It is the core plate-discipline input: low chase predicts walk rate and protects the hit tool against advanced sequencing. It stabilizes quickly and travels well across levels, so it's a leading indicator that a young hitter's approach will hold up against better pitching. League average is ~28-31%; sub-25% is plus discipline. Note the site defines the zone geometrically (a fixed rulebook rectangle), not by the called zone, so the metric is consistent across levels even though the enforced zone now differs by regime: MLB runs the ABS challenge system in 2026, AAA has used ABS regimes since 2023, and the Florida State League since 2022.
entries.formula: Chase% = out-of-zone swings / out-of-zone pitches × 100
entries.example: A 20-year-old at AA running a 22% Chase% has a discipline foundation that typically survives the jump to MLB sequencing.
entries.origin: Industry metric (O-Swing%). Plate-discipline rate from pitch tracking; the Statcast/Savant zone definition is used here.

entries.definition: Share of SWINGS that miss. For hitters, lower is better; for pitchers (induced whiff), higher is better.
entries.methodology: Whiff% = swings-and-misses ÷ total swings. For a hitter it measures bat-to-ball skill and underlies strikeout risk; for a pitcher it measures stuff (the rate at which his offerings are swung through). Distinct from K% (a plate-appearance outcome) - Whiff% is a per-swing rate and stabilizes faster. Hitter league average is ~24%; for a pitcher's primary pitch, 30%+ induced whiff is plus stuff.
entries.formula: Whiff% = swinging strikes / swings × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): swinging strikes per swing.

entries.definition: Share of swings on IN-zone pitches that make contact. The purest bat-to-ball / hit-tool signal.
entries.methodology: Z-Contact% = in-zone swings that make contact ÷ in-zone swings. By restricting to hittable pitches it isolates pure bat control from approach, so it's the tracked-data complement to the scouted Hit tool. Hitters who pair high Z-Contact with low Chase have the strongest hit-tool foundations. League average is ~85%; 90%+ is plus contact.
entries.formula: Z-Contact% = in-zone contact / in-zone swings × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. Plate-discipline rate popularized by FanGraphs (contact on in-zone swings).

entries.definition: Pitcher metric: share of pitches that are either called strikes OR whiffs. One number for 'how often this pitch beats the hitter.'
entries.methodology: CSW% = (called strikes + swinging strikes) ÷ total pitches. It folds stuff (whiffs) and command/deception (called strikes) into a single rate, and it stabilizes faster than K% because it counts every pitch, not just plate-appearance outcomes. League average is ~28%; 30%+ is a strong pitch, 32%+ is elite. Used as the high-signal modern pitcher input alongside K-BB%. Read the called-strike half with the strike-zone regime in mind: under the 2026 MLB ABS challenge system (and ABS regimes in AAA since 2023, the FSL since 2022) borderline calls are correctable, so framing and edge-stealing move fewer of them, and CSW% across those environments is not strictly comparable to a human-umpire baseline.
entries.formula: CSW% = (called strikes + whiffs) / pitches × 100
entries.origin: Industry metric. Called Strikes plus Whiffs, popularized by Alex Fast at Pitcher List.

entries.definition: Revolutions per minute on a pitch. Drives movement - high fastball spin → ride; high breaking-ball spin → sharper break.
entries.methodology: Spin rate (RPM) is a raw stuff input: on four-seamers, high active spin produces 'ride'/carry that beats hitters at the top of the zone; on breaking balls it produces tighter, later break. Spin only matters via the movement it creates (spin efficiency / spin axis), so it's an input to stuff models rather than a standalone grade. Typical four-seam spin is ~2,250 RPM; 2,500+ is high.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant), measured by Hawk-Eye tracking.

entries.definition: How far in front of the rubber a pitcher releases the ball (feet). More extension = less reaction time = effective velocity above the radar reading.
entries.methodology: Extension is the distance from the pitching rubber to the release point. Greater extension shortens the ball's perceived travel, adding 'effective velocity' - a 95-mph fastball with 7.0 ft of extension plays like ~96-97 to the hitter. It's why two pitchers with identical radar velocity can grade differently on stuff. League average is ~6.3 ft; 7.0+ ft is a meaningful add.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): how far off the rubber the ball is released.

entries.definition: Top running speed in feet per second on a player's fastest competitive runs. The tracked-data version of the Run tool.
entries.methodology: Sprint speed measures feet per second over a player's fastest one-second window on qualified runs. It is the objective complement to the scouted 20-80 Run grade and feeds defensive range and baserunning value. League average is ~27 ft/s; 28+ is plus, 30+ is elite (top-of-scale 70-80 run).
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant): feet per second in a runner's fastest one-second window.

entries.definition: Strikeout rate minus walk rate. A single pitcher command-and-miss number - the cleanest rate-stat summary of a pitcher's peripheral skill.
entries.methodology: K-BB% = K% − BB% (both as a share of batters faced). Subtracting walks from strikeouts captures the two outcomes a pitcher most controls in one figure, and it correlates with run prevention better than K/9 or BB/9 because it's denominated in batters faced rather than innings (innings are inflated by defense and sequencing luck). League-average starters sit ~13-14%; 18%+ is plus, 22%+ is elite.
entries.formula: K-BB% = K% − BB%
entries.example: A starter at 30% K% and 7% BB% posts a 23% K-BB% - front-of-rotation peripheral skill regardless of a noisy ERA.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: Level-anchored offensive index for a MiLB season. 100 is the league average for that level and season. As of 2026-07-31 the site computes this as wRC+ vs level, not OPS+: the rate is a linear-weight wOBA rather than an OPS ratio, and the baseline is a plate-appearance-weighted pool of the WHOLE league rather than an unweighted mean of the prospects this site happens to track.
entries.methodology: Fixed FanGraphs-shape linear weights, rescaled inside each level-season so the pool's mean wOBA equals its OBP, then indexed against that pool and shrunk toward it by plate appearances (K = 200 PA, which holds the previous chip's shrink strength constant rather than retuning it inside a metric swap). The baseline change matters as much as the metric one: the old tracked-prospect baseline ran 7 to 8 percent low at Double-A and High-A (.703 against a true .752, .708 against .767), so the retired chip flattered every hitter at those levels. Measured across 1,972 served hitters the new chip sits about 2 points lower on the median and is slightly tighter, and it genuinely reorders: 8.5 percent of pairs swap. Coverage is 100 percent. Components come from the same MLB StatsAPI response the site already fetches for MiLB seasons.
entries.formula: OPS+ = 100 × OPS_adj / lgOPS,  where OPS_adj = (AB·OPS + K·lgOPS)/(AB + K) shrinks toward the level mean (K = 170 AB).  Computed vs the player's level.
entries.origin: Industry metric. OPS+ in the Bill James tradition (Baseball-Reference implements the league version). Here it is computed relative to the player's minor-league level and carries no park adjustment.

entries.definition: Career WAR an org's graduates produced per $1M of signing-bonus spend. The headline capital-efficiency leaf of the Financial branch.
entries.methodology: WAR per $M = total career WAR of an org's graduates ÷ total signing-bonus dollars (draft + IFA), in $M. It is the purest bang-for-buck measure of an org's amateur acquisition + development: did the money spent turn into MLB production? Lagging (WAR only accrues after debut), so it's gated at ≥3 grads with both bonus and career-WAR on file. Anchored across the 30 orgs into the Financial composite.
entries.formula: WAR per $M = Σ career_WAR(grads) / (Σ signing_bonus_USD / 1,000,000)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Per-year dollar surplus on an org's graduates: current AAV minus the signing bonus amortized over six cost-controlled years.
entries.methodology: For each graduate with both Spotrac contract data and a signing bonus on file, surplus per year = current AAV − (signing bonus ÷ 6). It captures whether the org is extracting cheap production from the six cost-controlled years a prospect provides before free agency - the core economic reason prospects are assets. Averaged across qualifying grads and z-anchored into the Financial branch.
entries.formula: per-year surplus = current_AAV − (signing_bonus / 6)
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The org-level roll-up of its active prospects' $DvM+ - development of surplus dollars, indexed to 100 = league mean.
entries.methodology: Aggregates the $DvM+ of an org's active prospects (development-vs-mean applied to projected surplus dollars rather than raw FV) into one 100-anchored org figure. It rewards systems that are growing the dollar value of the talent they already hold, not just its scouting grade. Feeds the Financial branch alongside the realized-money leaves (WAR/$M, contract surplus).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Travel the consensus board to any past monthly snapshot, or diff two dates for a changelog of risers, fallers, new entries, graduates, and grade changes.
entries.methodology: Each monthly run snapshots the board (rank + consensus FV + the Arkmetric family per prospect) into metric_snapshots. The Time Machine reconstructs the board as it stood at any past snapshot and can diff two dates - producing an explicit changelog of who rose, fell, debuted/graduated, or changed grade. URL-shareable, so a specific board state or diff can be linked.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Export a shareable graphic - a prospect card, farm card, list, or card pack - as a PNG (or a short animated clip), with rarity treatment matching the list.
entries.methodology: Generate GFX rasterizes an on-theme graphic for sharing: single-prospect cards (compact / detailed / scouting / stats / card-back templates), farm cards, ranked-list boards, and multi-card 'packs'. Cards carry the FV-tier rarity frame, the FV history chart, tool radar, Statcast sliders, and surplus. Exports are 2× resolution; an animated WebM shows the holographic foil. The blob is pre-rendered so Copy/Download/Share are near-instant.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A configurable plot/query builder: any X/Y metric, color + size encodings, log scales, filters, brush-to-zoom, a shareable URL config, and a GFX export.
entries.methodology: The Scatterplots view lets you build an arbitrary two-axis plot over any prospect cohort (MiLB, debuted, draft, overseas, IFA, or farm systems): pick X/Y from any metric, add color and size encodings, toggle log scales, apply org/level/position + per-axis threshold filters, brush to zoom, and highlight/search individual players. The full configuration is encoded in the URL so a specific query is shareable.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A personal, locally-saved set of starred prospects, filterable and exportable as a GFX card pack.
entries.methodology: Starring a prospect adds them to a Watchlist stored in the browser (localStorage - nothing leaves the device). The list is filterable like any board and can be exported as a Generate GFX card pack, so a personal shortlist becomes a shareable sheet.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Curated movement buckets - Risers, Fallers, Rebounders, and breakout/upside flags - with the driver signals that put each prospect there.
entries.methodology: Spotlights classifies recent prospect movement into buckets (Risers / Fallers / Rebounders) using consensus-FV velocity confirmed or contradicted by performance signals (RPS+, SC+, tool velocity), and surfaces the specific driver chips behind each placement. The spotlight age cap gates excessively-old prospects out so an aging hot stretch doesn't read as a prospect breakout.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: FV-keyed collectible treatment on prospect photos: shine (45) → foil (50) → chrome (55-60) → holo (61-69) → legendary (70+). Same logic on the list and in Generate GFX.
entries.methodology: Rarity maps the prospect's FV tier to a photo border/effect, so the rarest prospects read instantly as collectible cards. Thresholds: FV 45 = shine (static gold), 50 = foil (silver shimmer), 55-60 = chrome, 61-69 = holo (rainbow), 70+ = legendary (rainbow + breathing glow); below 45 = a plain team-color frame. The exact same FV→tier logic drives the prospect-list headshots and the Generate GFX cards, so a prospect's rarity is consistent everywhere (in GFX the live animation is captured as a faithful static frame so it survives PNG export).
entries.visual: 70legendary → holo → chrome → foil → shine
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Press ⌘K (Mac) or Ctrl+K to look up any glossary term - or jump to any prospect - from anywhere on the site.
entries.methodology: The quick-search palette is the site-wide entry point to the glossary single-source-of-truth: type any metric name or alias to see its definition inline and open the full entry. It also resolves prospect names for fast navigation. Opens with ⌘K / Ctrl+K (or the / key) and is dismissable with Escape.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Predicted total contract guarantee for a free agent, from the market model - on the DEFERRAL-ADJUSTED NPV basis (a 97%-deferred sticker is not the same liability as level cash; schedules in the curated deferral ledger discount at the platform 9% rate, no-schedule deals keep their sticker). What teams WILL pay in present-value terms, not what the production is worth. Formerly displayed as mGuarantee.
entries.methodology: projGuarantee is the market model: a transparent two-stage regression (contract length first, then log-guarantee given length) trained only on the 2014-15 to present FA-signing corpus, with age, projected year-1 bWAR, position group, qualifying-offer status, class supply, the winter $/WAR level (carried forward ex-ante), nearest-comps anchors, and economic anchors (discounted projected WAR x $/WAR; prime-years x quality). Predictions clamp to a 2.5x envelope around the comps median and blend toward comps in the megadeal regime. P10-P90 bands are empirical residual quantiles from the forward-chained backtest. The model beat the nearest-comps baseline on guarantee, AAV and years across nine held-out winters (Gate 2 on the Model Accountability page). Phase 2 (2026-06): targets, comps anchors and the winter $/WAR series all moved to the NPV basis; Gate 2 re-ran and improved (guarantee MAE 10.06 vs comps 11.19). A LightGBM challenger with monotonic economic constraints LOST to this model on all three ship criteria at n=1,199 (committed to the artifact) - the transparent two-stage OLS retains. The flat-5% $/WAR escalation also survived its challenge: fitted trend forecasts lost the forward-chained eval (MAPE 0.122/0.132 vs 0.102).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Predicted average annual value: projGuarantee / projLength, with its own P10-P90 band. Formerly displayed as mAAV.
entries.methodology: Both framings of a contract are projected: the per-year price (projAAV) and the total value / length (projGuarantee / projLength). projAAV bands ride the guarantee band at the point-estimate term.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Predicted contract length in years (P10-P90 banded), from a log-years model with comps stacking and a prime-years-remaining term. Formerly displayed as mYears.
entries.methodology: Contract length is modeled before money (teams trade years against AAV). The stage predicts log(years) with curvature terms (WAR squared, age x WAR), prime years remaining (max(0, 30 - age) - the buyable seasons behind long deals), and the nearest-comps median length stacked as a feature; it beat the comps baseline 0.441 vs 0.485 MAE across nine held-out winters (Gate 2, fa_mkt_v2).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The surfaces render a plain-English VERDICT - value (projected underpaid), market (priced about right), overpay (projected overpaid) - backed by Deal+, the 100-scale index of rational value against price.
entries.methodology: Deal+ = 100 x rational value / predicted (or actual) guarantee. Verdict band edges are EMPIRICALLY CENTERED on the 2015-2026 corpus terciles, not symmetric around 100: Deal+ under convex pricing is right-skewed (corpus p33 = 75, median = 110, p67 = 159 on the Phase-2 NPV basis), so value is >= 160, overpay is < 75, market is the middle tercile. Each verdict named exactly a third of twelve winters of real contracts; a class that skews one way against these fixed bands is information.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Rational value minus predicted market price - the gap the module exists to surface.
entries.methodology: Two independently derived numbers, never conflated: RATIONAL VALUE (what the projected production is worth in NPV) and PREDICTED MARKET PRICE (what teams will actually pay, from the market model). Contract Surplus ($) is rational minus market. Positive = the market is expected to underprice the player. The retrospective ledger applies the same lens backward: realized bWAR x each season's estimated $/WAR minus prorated money paid, for every MLB free-agent deal since 2014-15.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The dollar cost of forfeited draft picks (and intl pool money) when signing a qualifying-offer free agent.
entries.methodology: Signing a QO-attached free agent forfeits draft picks per the CBA compensation matrix (rule-versioned; CBT payors forfeit their 2nd- and 5th-highest picks plus $1M of international pool). The module prices each forfeited slot using the platform's OWN draft research: median consensus FV at the slot mapped through the prospect surplus curve. Because rational value and pick values share the same 9% NPV currency, the tax subtracts directly.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The NPV of a free agent's projected WAR path: each season priced CONVEXLY through the platform's tier curve at the winter's ex-ante FA $/WAR level, escalated per season and discounted at the platform's 9% rate. One of the platform's two independently derived numbers - what the production is worth, never what the market will pay.
entries.methodology: Rational value shares the same NPV currency as PROSPX prospect surplus - and, since v2, the same CONVEX season pricing (value_framework's tier curve, rescaled to the winter's $/WAR level): a 1-WAR season and the third win of a 3-WAR season are not the same product, and a flat rate graded the entire bottom of the class as a bargain (measured: class median Deal+ 220 under flat pricing). It is deliberately computed with no reference to the market model: the gap between the two numbers (Contract Surplus) only means something because neither side peeks at the other. The winter $/WAR level it prices at is the NPV-basis signings-implied series (deferral-adjusted numerator) carried forward at the measured-best flat 5%.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The 10th-90th percentile range shown around every FA market prediction. Empirical residual quantiles from the forward-chained backtest - not parametric intervals, which failed the coverage gate (0.858 vs the 0.75-0.85 target) and were rejected.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Probability that an option-holding player actually reaches the free-agent class, from a documented v1 heuristic: the option price against the player's market anchor through a logistic. Mutual options carry a fixed empirical prior; rows with no anchor show no number rather than a guess.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The 2022 CBA expired 2026-12-01, so every 2027 threshold, tax band, and QO figure is the last known rule carried forward, not a bargained number. Every surface that consumes one of these figures carries the carry-forward flag rather than presenting it as settled.

The per-winter price of a win implied by that winter's actual FA signings: guaranteed dollars over projected WAR delivered, carried forward ex-ante so a prediction never sees its own winter. Distinct from the PROSPX $/WAR (tiered) figure, which is a 3-tier rolling market price used for prospect valuation - the two serve different models and are not interchangeable.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Disclosure badge on FA projections whose platform season is missing or injury-shortened - below 30% of a role-aware full season, scaled by how much of the season has elapsed. A projection riding old seasons is the model's weakest case (the Burnes/Bieber rehab class), flagged rather than hidden.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The five 0-1 scores behind every FA team fit: need (displacement WAR gap at the position, discounted when a near-ETA PROSPX prospect blocks it; MLB incumbents block through the gap itself and are NAMED in the blocked-by list), window (marginal playoff leverage at the club's baseline wins), afford (CBT-basis tax space against the predicted AAV, with a documented floor for habitual taxpayers), park (batted-side park factor - deliberately the smallest weight, a tiebreaker not a driver), and behavior (WILL they spend: biggest-ever guarantee vs this price, recent 3-winter outlay, $100M-deal participation).
entries.methodology: v2 reweight: need 0.31 / window 0.19 / afford 0.22 / park 0.04 / behavior 0.24. Park was cut from 0.12 after the measured failure mode - the most suppressive park topped EVERY pitcher's fit list because park alone separated otherwise-similar clubs. Afford reads Spotrac's CBT-basis tax space (the number front offices budget against) and floors at 0.4 for clubs over the line that keep signing nine-figure deals; behavior blends deal-scale history (0.5), recency-weighted three-winter FA outlay (0.3), and $100M-deal count (0.2). Blocked-by names both kinds of blocker: PX = a near-ETA PROSPX prospect (FV >= 50), MLB = a contracted incumbent projecting >= 2.5 WAR at the slot the signing would displace.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Winter events (signings, option decisions, qualifying offers) are dated the day the pipeline first observed them, because the source publishes terms without dates. Stamps are append-only and never revised - the same no-lookahead discipline the models train under.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The FA module's two shipping blockers: Gate 1, the projection engine against ten held-out seasons (beat the naive baseline; P10-P90 coverage in 0.75-0.85); Gate 2, the market model against nine forward-chained winters (beat the nearest-comps baseline on guarantee, AAV, and years). Both verdicts render verbatim on the Free Agency Model Accountability page - misses included.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The most similar real historical contracts to a free agent's profile, by standardized feature distance over the 2014-15-to-present signing corpus. Always actual deals, never fabricated; they anchor the market model and appear on every board row so a prediction can be sanity-checked against what comparable players actually signed for.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A Marcel-style weighted-rates projection (5/3/2 recency weights) with hitter ISO blended toward Savant xISO (2015+), mapped to bWAR through a fitted rate-to-WAR model and decayed along survivorship-corrected aging curves fit on the 2000-2026 corpus. v2: multi-year decay walks REGRESSED-rate curves - raw observed deltas bundle aging with luck regression, and chaining them double-counted the regression (measured: the horizon-5 star tail collapsed to a 0.06 predicted/actual ratio). Power and finesse pitchers age on their own curves; hitter power/contact cohorts were measured and parked (season-ISO selection re-injects reversion).
entries.methodology: Beyond Gate 1 (next-season), the multi-year decay is now measured by a forward-chained horizon backtest (proj_eval.py, bases 2017-2021): the v2 regressed-rate curves doubled the horizon-5 >=3-WAR tail ratio (0.06 to 0.12) and cut star bias from -1.34 to -0.64 WAR while Gate 1 improved. Phase 1 (2026-06): horizons 1-5 are served by proj_lgbm_v1 - LightGBM quantile models (P10/P25/P50/P75/P90 per horizon) stacked ON the Marcel champion (its prediction rides as a feature, so the trees learn its residuals), with no zero floor on the bands (the measured cause of the old coverage collapse). Shipped under best-model-wins after beating the champion on dev bases, the Gate-1 target seasons (h1 MAE 0.557 vs 0.627) and a touched-once 2022-2024 holdout; the Marcel+aging champion remains the fallback, the stacking feature, and the shape for horizons 6+. Disclosed: long-horizon star medians run ~0.2 WAR below the champion (zero-inflated labels), with equal star MAE.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Park- and league-adjusted ERA scaled so 100 = MLB average; lower is better. 90 reads as 10% better than league; the run-prevention twin of FIP-.
entries.origin: Industry metric. The ERA- park- and league-adjusted index, implemented by FanGraphs (100 = average, lower is better). Here it is level-relative.

entries.definition: On-base average with each event weighted by its actual run value (a walk is worth less than a double, which OBP ignores). Scaled to look like OBP: ~.320 is league average, .400 elite.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Created by Tom Tango (The Book); implemented by FanGraphs. It weights each offensive event by its average run value.

entries.definition: Lifecycle markers on module names site-wide: α = newly launched, numbers may still shift as the model matures; β = established but in beta. The bordered chip on a module masthead and the superscript in navs are the same marker.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The homepage event feed and scrolling ticker: debuts, promotions, trades, IL moves, real FV changes, and free-agency winter events, each dated and color-coded by type. FV items are real grade changes only; composite movement scores are not shown as news.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The set of currently-tracked, non-graduated MiLB prospects that every ranking, farm grade, and Arkmetric is computed over. Pool integrity is a platform invariant: MLB-side modules (Free Agency) read prospect data read-only and may not write into it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Every projected WAR path ships three variants: mean, floor (P10) and ceiling (P90). Veterans take the Gate-1 empirical year-1 residual quantile for their reliability bucket, applied to the year-1 WAR and decayed along the SAME aging curves - uncertainty propagates the way talent does. Prospects take the 10th/90th-percentile OUTCOME BUCKET of the calibrated P(bucket|FV) categorical: a prospect's downside is the bust outcome, not a symmetric band.
entries.methodology: The quantiles come from the committed Gate-1 artifact (fa_gate1_eval.json band_quantiles, empirical per side x exposure tier), so the bands carry the measured 0.80 P10-P90 coverage rather than a parametric assumption. Surplus buckets price the floor/ceiling paths through the same convex curve as the mean - the surplus range on a player card is the same machinery, never a separate model. Since Phase 1 the veteran floor/mean/ceiling come directly from the quantile heads (empirically trained on horizon residual distributions, negatives included) rather than decaying a single year-1 quantile.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The /projections/ surface: the FA module's Gate-1-validated projection engine applied to every MLB player with recent history - five-year bWAR paths with floor/mean/ceiling probability buckets - plus PROSPX prospects joining at their projected ETA via the calibrated FV outcome model.
entries.methodology:
Veterans: the same Marcel engine, aging curves and fitted WAR map the FA class board prices contracts with (one engine, gate-checked once, consumed twice). Prospects: P(bucket|FV) x per-bucket WAR trajectories scaled by FV and shaped by projected debut age - bust-inclusive means, outcome-bucket floor/ceiling. Seasons are priced through the convex tier curve at the ex-ante FA $/WAR level, escalating per season; veteran surplus exists ONLY on salary-known (Spotrac-contracted) seasons and discounts at the platform 9%; arb/pre-arb seasons carry projections but no surplus claim. Prospect surplus is the platform surplus value - never a parallel number.

Team Outlook win totals are retro-backtested and calibrated (2026-06-12). Each roster sums the engine's mean year-1 projections (the quantile-model point used on player pages is median-like and is never summed), plus a depth pool of sub-floor players and age-cohort corrections fit on 2022-24 backtest residuals and gated on a held-out 2025. The league sums to 2,430 wins with a near-zero remainder. In the 2022-25 backtest the roll-up's team MAE ran 7.3-10.2 wins and beat a prior-season-wins carry-forward in three of four seasons; the full accounting ships in team_outlook_eval.json.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The accountability tab on the MLB Projections module: every projection model's champion, the baseline it had to beat, the metric, the measured held-out result, and a note on what is not yet scoreable. The verdicts are read straight from the platform's model registry, refreshed monthly; no claim is shown that has not been graded against history.
entries.methodology: Each model is evaluated by forward-chaining: fit on data through year Y-1, score the untouched year Y, repeat, and report pooled and per-year accuracy against a stated baseline. A model only earns the validated verdict when that held-out backtest beats its baseline on the pre-registered metric; if a piece is only partially measured (short window, descriptive, or live-pending) it ships provisional and is labeled as such. The committed eval artifacts (data/*_eval.json) carry the full tables; the registry (data/model_registry.json) carries the one-line verdict and the methodology disclosures, and a test (test_methodology_freshness.py) forces every registry model to map to the glossary entry that documents it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The four-way honesty label every model in the registry carries: validated (a forward-chained backtest beats the baseline), provisional (measured, but only partially - short window or descriptive), unvalidated (a predictive claim with no measurement yet, listed so it cannot hide), or deprecated (failed validation, retired).
entries.methodology: Verdicts are hand-committed alongside their eval artifact, not auto-derived: validated requires the artifact to exist and beat its baseline on the pre-registered metric; unvalidated must NOT carry an artifact (it is the audit hit list). A monthly refresh re-stamps freshness (artifact age) but never silently upgrades a verdict.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Grading a model on history it never saw at fit time: the model is trained only on seasons through year Y-1, then scored on the untouched year Y, walking forward one year at a time. No-lookahead by construction, so the measured error is what a user would actually have gotten in real time.
entries.methodology: Curves, weights and maps are refit per target year on data through Y-1 (the Gate-1 pattern), predictions are compared to realized outcomes, and accuracy is pooled across folds plus reported per year. A held-out season (one fold deliberately untouched during any tuning) is the cleanest read; the rest are dev folds. Team-level reads assign each player to his ACTUAL season team so the engine's error is isolated from roster churn (disclosed).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A season (or fold) deliberately kept out of every tuning decision and looked at only once, at the very end, to confirm a model generalizes. Because it never influenced a single knob, its error is the least-biased estimate of real-world accuracy; a model that wins on dev folds but loses the holdout does not ship.
entries.methodology: Distinct from cross-validation dev folds, which are used repeatedly while iterating. The projections engine reports a touched-once 2022-2024 holdout for veteran WAR paths and a held-out 2025 for team wins; out-years whose labels have not matured yet are flagged as not-yet-scoreable rather than counted.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The pending live scoreboard for a projection whose target has not happened yet: the model's number is logged now and graded later, when the real outcome lands, against a stated baseline. It is the difference between a backtest (history) and a genuine out-of-sample bet on the future.
entries.methodology: Team Outlook win totals are the standing example: only the first projected season is forward-gateable, scored as MAE versus actual standings when that season completes (baseline = prior-season wins carry-forward); out-years are a competitive trajectory, not a scored forecast. The gate status stays pending until the season finishes, then the result is committed whatever it says.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The average size of a model's misses, in the units of whatever it predicts: the mean of |actual - predicted| across every case. Lower is better, and unlike a correlation it is in real units - a team-wins MAE of 7.7 means the projected record is off by about eight wins on average.
entries.methodology: Reported alongside bias (the average signed error - whether the model runs systematically high or low) and, for the bands, coverage (the share of actuals that land inside the P10-P90 interval, target ~80%). MAE penalizes large and small misses linearly, so it resists the pull of the heavy WAR tail that would dominate a squared-error metric.
entries.origin: Standard baseball statistic (no single creator); defined here for reference.

entries.definition: The behavioral profile on each farm system’s Tendencies tab: promotion aggressiveness, draft position/trait preferences, pitch identity of developed arms, per-tool development rates, international pool strategy (quality vs quantity), trade profile (volume, prospect-capital direction, quality-vs-depth, cash considerations), draft-pool allocation, and IL burden - every value league-relative.
entries.methodology: Each axis is computed from the platform’s own records (grade history 2017-present, signed draft picks 2021-present, IFA classes, the trade ledger, MLB transaction text) and expressed as a z-score across the 30 orgs; verdict labels only fire at |z| ≥ 0.5. Tool development uses SAME-SOURCE snapshot pairs ≥ 60 days apart inside one org, so cross-source disagreement never counts as development. Pitch identity profiles the MLB arsenals of the players an org developed (per-pitch usage history is not archived yet, so conversion ledgers like four-seam → sinker are a documented v2). Cash-consideration direction is parsed from official transaction descriptions.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How far a drafted player has outrun his draft slot, on the Draft tab's Overperformers board.
