entries.definition: A hitter's DESERVED offensive rate on the HEM+ scale: HEM+ computed from Savant expected wOBA (xwOBA) instead of actual results, so it reflects contact quality rather than how the balls happened to fall. Luck is xHEM+ minus HEM+.
entries.methodology: xHEM+ = 100 times the hitter's Savant expected wOBA over the plate-appearance-weighted pool average, on the same 100-anchored scale as HEM+. Expected wOBA is built from the launch conditions of each batted ball (exit velocity and angle), so it strips the batting-average-on-balls-in-play and sequencing luck baked into actual wOBA. Validated out of sample: forward-chained over eight season-pairs 2016-2025 (excluding 2020, 1871 pairs), expected wOBA predicts a hitter's next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.45 vs 0.41 for actual wOBA, with the gap confidence floor above zero -- so it is the more forward-stable talent signal. It is a COMPANION for tracked hitters (Statcast is MLB-only and needs a real sample, 100+ tracked plate appearances), not the population-complete HEM+. Luck greater than zero means a hitter is under-performing his contact (room to bounce back); less than zero means he is over-performing (due to regress). Accountability artifact: data/xhem_plus_eval.json.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: The best single-number read on a hitter's NEXT-year offense: a 70/30 blend of Savant expected wOBA and the HEM+ skill core, shown on the HEM+ scale (100 = the average hitter in the tracked pool). Expected wOBA carries the contact-quality signal; the light HEM+ leg adds back the shrunk plate-discipline signal that contact quality alone misses.
entries.methodology: Within the season, the hitter's Savant expected wOBA and his unrounded HEM+ core are each standardized over the tracked pool (100+ Savant plate appearances), combined 70/30, and mapped back onto the HEM+ ratio display scale by the pool's own HEM+ location and spread -- a rank-preserving transform, so the shipped ordering IS the validated ordering. Validated out of sample: forward-chained over eight season-pairs 2016-2025 (excluding 2020, 1871 pairs), the blend predicts a hitter's next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.466 vs 0.454 for expected wOBA alone, with the paired bootstrap gap confidence floor above zero under the pre-registered convention (the newer clustered harness reads the same edge as positive but within noise, reported alongside). A competing multi-year decayed candidate failed its gate, so this single-season blend is the incumbent forward column. Like xHEM+, it is a COMPANION for tracked hitters (Statcast is MLB-only and needs a real sample), not the population-complete HEM+. Accountability artifact: data/xhem_plus_eval.json (X-H5 block).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A hitter's projected NEXT-season wOBA from the site's FA-engine Marcel, the same validated projection engine that prices the FA class board and drives MLB Projections. Read it like wOBA: roughly .310 is league average, .370 is a star season, .400 and up is elite. Where HEM+ and the xHEM+ family grade THIS season, pWOBA is the engine's best single-number forecast of next season's offensive rate.
entries.methodology: The engine projects each wOBA component (walk rate, strikeout rate, isolated power, BABIP, home runs per plate appearance) as a Marcel-style weighted average of the trailing three seasons (5/3/2 recency weights, exposure-weighted), regresses each toward the league mean, blends observed ISO toward Savant xISO where tracking exists, and ages every rate along survivorship-corrected aging curves; the components are then assembled back into a wOBA with fixed run-value weights. Validated for exactly this job by the T1-10 projection gate (data/phem_marcel_lite_eval.json): over predictor seasons 2021-2024 (918 out-of-sample year pairs) the engine's projected wOBA predicts next-year wOBA at a Spearman correlation of 0.5189 vs 0.4939 for the best trailing-average incumbent, with the paired-bootstrap confidence floor above zero and the result confirmed under the newer clustered harness. A purpose-built multi-year challenger lost the same gate, so this column re-anchors the existing engine rather than adding a new model. Shown for tracked hitters with a real recent MLB sample (100 or more plate appearances in the trailing three seasons); the in-progress season is exposure-weighted like any partial sample. Current boards only: a past season's board has no next season to project.
entries.origin: Projection column from the site's FA-engine Marcel. The Marcel weighted-rates framework is Tom Tango's; the engine that produces this number (survivorship-corrected aging curves, Savant xISO blend, league re-anchoring) is an Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: SEM+ over the trailing three seasons, innings-weighted, shown with the pitcher's pool percentile. Same starter run-prevention scale as SEM+ (100 = average qualified starter). Read it as a steadier version of the single-season number, not a stronger forecast.
entries.methodology: Each of the trailing three seasons' SEM+ is averaged with innings-pitched weights, a steadier read than one starter season. It did NOT reliably beat the single-season number in the forward test: three-year forward Spearman 0.414 versus 0.392 for one year on the same starters, but the gap is not statistically separable (95% interval runs negative). So it ships as a steadiness companion with the numbers published, not a more predictive replacement.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The total change in a player's team win probability across every play he was involved in -- credited to the BATTER on offense and to the PITCHER on defense (opposite signs on the same play). A counting stat of in-the-moment impact, inflated by the leverage of the spots the player was in.
entries.methodology: Summed from the MLB win-probability feed: each play's change in the pitcher's team win expectancy, credited to the pitcher on the mound. Because a run prevented in a tie game in the ninth moves win probability far more than the same out in a blowout, WPA rewards high-leverage usage as much as performance. Batter WPA is the negation of the pitcher's on the same play (the batting team gains what the fielding team loses), summed over the player's plate appearances; per-play home-team win-probability-added, sign-flipped to the involved player's team.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Win Probability Added, from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango and coauthors, The Book); implemented by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: Win Probability Added with the leverage of each play divided out, so it measures performance independent of how important the situations were. The leverage-stripped companion to WPA.
entries.origin: Industry metric. WPA divided by leverage index, a context-neutral wins measure from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango).

entries.definition: How important a game situation is, based on inning, score, outs, and baserunners, where 1.0 is an average situation. Created by Tom Tango. Below 0.85 is low leverage, 2.0 and up is high leverage.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Leverage Index, created by Tom Tango (The Book): how much the current game state can swing win probability, 1.0 = average.

entries.definition: Per-appearance reliever outcomes. A Shutdown adds at least 0.06 to the team's win probability in an outing; a Meltdown subtracts at least that much. Shutdowns minus Meltdowns is a cleaner reliever record than saves and holds.
entries.origin: Industry metric. Reliever WPA thresholds proposed by Tom Tango and implemented by FanGraphs.

entries.definition: The leverage ladder of a bullpen, assigned from entry leverage (gmLI) and usage. Closer finishes games at the highest leverage; High-leverage and Setup pitch the tightest middle innings; Middle relief works average spots; Long and Mop-up cover multi-inning or low-stakes work.
A 0 to 100 candidate score for how well a current reliever would profile as a starter. Higher means a better fit. It is a screen for finding candidates, not a probability of success.
entries.methodology: A transparent weighted blend anchored on the role-structural signal the sabermetric research points to: arsenal depth, because a starter has to survive a lineup three times, so a third and fourth pitch matter most. The rest of the blend is command (walk rate), how fastball-reliant the arm is, platoon-neutrality, contact quality, and stuff. Fastball velocity is projected down about one mile per hour for the longer role. The weights are priors from the literature, not fitted. The repaired per-direction backtest does not validate the ranking within this direction: pre-conversion FIT ran negative against realized WAR change on the small reliever-to-starter sample (rho about -0.21 on 25 gated events), so treat the list as a structural shortlist of arms with starter traits, not a forecast of who converts best.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A 0 to 100 candidate score for how well a current starter's stuff would play up in a one-inning relief role. Higher means a better fit.
entries.methodology: The traits that hurt a starter are exactly what make a good reliever: a thin, fastball-heavy arsenal that leaks runs the third time through a lineup is fine for one inning. So this score rewards a dominant putaway pitch, projected relief velocity (about one mile per hour up in short bursts), stuff quality, and the times-through-order leakage that is the complement of arsenal depth. A display-only projected relief REM+ shows roughly what the arm might post as a reliever. This direction carries a validated directional signal: in the repaired per-direction backtest, pre-conversion FIT out-ranked every same-event baseline against realized WAR change (rho about +0.29 on 61 gated events, with the gap over the best baseline positive at the 95 percent floor).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The model behind the Alchemy Lab: two candidate scores (RP->SP FIT and SP->RP FIT) plus a history of past role conversions that doubles as the backtest set. Backtest evidence is per direction: SP->RP is validated, RP->SP is a structural screen.
entries.methodology: Conversions are detected from season starting shares across 2018 to 2026 (a role flip between qualified seasons). The primary outcome is the change in realized Baseball-Reference WAR from the pre-role season to the post-role season, scored within each direction and never pooled; a held-the-role label (at least one full closed season in the new role) is kept as a sensitivity check. In the repaired 2026 harness the SP->RP direction passes its gate: pre-conversion FIT out-ranks every same-event baseline against realized WAR change (rho about +0.29, 61 gated events). The RP->SP direction fails it (rho about -0.21 on 25 events), so that list ships as a structural screen whose ranking the backtest does not validate. The sample is small and selection-biased, since we only observe pitchers teams chose to convert, so neither score is a success-probability forecast and the model ships provisional with a downgraded registry verdict.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How many distinct pitches a pitcher throws at least ten percent of the time. The single most important trait for surviving a lineup multiple times, and the structural core of the RP->SP FIT score.

The tendency for a pitcher to get worse each time he faces the same lineup in a game. It is the mechanism that separates starters from relievers: a deep, varied arsenal blunts it, while a thin fastball-heavy mix collapses by the third time through. A reliever only faces the order once.
entries.origin: Industry concept. The times-through-order penalty, quantified by Mitchel Lichtman and coauthors (The Book).

entries.definition: The change in fastball velocity when a pitcher moves between roles. A starter stretching out loses about a mile per hour; a pitcher moving to one-inning relief gains about that much. Rigorous studies put the central number near one mile per hour, larger for pure power arms, so the Lab projects it modestly rather than assuming the folklore of three or four.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A pitcher's single best swing-and-miss pitch, measured by whiff rate. A dominant putaway pitch is what lets a starter's stuff play up in a one-inning relief role, so it drives the SP->RP FIT score.

The gap in results a pitcher allows to left-handed versus right-handed hitters (here, the OPS-against difference). A flat split means he can face a full lineup without being hidden from one side, which supports starting. A large split is a conversion blocker.

The set of non-pitcher positions a player has real game experience at, drawn from actual MLB and MiLB fielding logs rather than a scout's projected multi-position tag. A wider Versa profile means more lineup and roster flexibility.
entries.methodology: Versa is built from StatsAPI game fielding, not a reported position string. A position counts when the player has meaningful exposure there: at least 10 games, or at least 5 starts at that spot. Designated hitter is excluded because it is not a fielding position. The result is the honest, game-backed set of places a player has actually stood, so a listed shortstop who has logged real innings at second and third shows all three.
entries.formula: Position qualifies at >= 10 G or >= 5 GS at that spot; DH excluded
entries.example: A shortstop with 40 G at SS, 12 G at 2B, and 6 GS at 3B shows Versa: SS / 2B / 3B.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A draft prospect's board rank expressed as an index where 100 is the middle of the class and higher is a more valued prospect. It starts from the consensus board position and is nudged a few points by a college-performance signal, so a standout amateur season can move a prospect a little off his rank-derived baseline.
entries.methodology: DS+ maps a prospect's consensus draft rank to roughly a 70 to 130 index (best of class near 130, back of the board near 70), computed on the raw fractional consensus ranks so tightly bunched prospects stay distinct. A z-scored college-performance term then nudges the value up or down by up to about six points, and the result is clamped. It is a heuristic stock indicator, not a validated projection. This is different from Draft Overperformance, which compares realized FV to slot after the fact.
entries.formula: DS+ = rank-to-index (about 70-130) + college-performance nudge (up to about +-6), clamped
entries.example: A prospect ranked 8th in a class of 250 with a strong statistical spring might carry a DS+ near 126.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: How much better a pitcher holds opposite-handed hitters than same-handed hitters, the reverse of the normal platoon pattern. A reverse split is a rare hidden strength that supports a full-lineup starter role, since the batters who would normally platoon against him do not get their edge.
entries.methodology: For a right-handed pitcher the index is his OPS-against versus righties minus his OPS-against versus lefties (mirrored for a lefty). A value above zero means he allows more to his own hand than to the opposite hand, a reverse split. The radar flags a reverse split above 0.03 and an extreme split at or beyond 0.15, and only counts pitchers with at least 100 batters faced on the lighter side so small-sample noise does not surface as a hidden strength.
entries.formula: reverse index = own-hand OPS-against minus opposite-hand OPS-against (RHP: vsR minus vsL); reverse if > 0.03; requires >= 100 TBF
entries.example: A righty who allows a .720 OPS to righties but only .560 to lefties has a reverse index of +0.16: he neutralizes the opposite-handed bats that would normally platoon against him.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A 0 to 100 read on whether a pitching prospect's tools fit a starting role or a relief role, built only from scout grades (arsenal depth and command). It is a shape screen, not a stuff-physics projection: it flags prospects whose listed role conflicts with what their tool grades suggest.
entries.methodology: Starter Shape scores a prospect pitcher from his 20-80 scout grades alone. It rewards arsenal depth (the count of distinct pitches graded 55 or better, since a starter needs a third weapon to turn a lineup over three times) and command, blended roughly 60/40. A high score on a reliever-labeled prospect, or a low score on a starter-labeled one, is flagged as a role mismatch on the PAL Prospect Watch. It uses no minor-league stats, so it is a descriptive shape read, not a validated outcome model.
entries.formula: Starter Shape = 0.60 x arsenal-depth score (pitches graded >= 55) + 0.40 x command score, on scout grades only
entries.example: A prospect graded FB 60 / SL 55 / CB 45 / CH 40 with 40 command has thin depth and light command, a low Starter Shape, so a starter-labeled version is flagged as profiling in relief.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Expected wOBA: what a hitter's contact and plate results are worth based on how the ball was struck, stripping out defense and luck.
entries.methodology: xwOBA estimates wOBA from the quality of contact (exit velocity and launch angle) plus strikeouts and walks, using the run values of each outcome. xwOBAcon is the contact-only version. It answers what a hitter deserved rather than what fell in. The value shown on player cards is our estimate from the tracking inputs available, so read it as our reconstruction, not the official Savant figure.
entries.origin: Industry metric. MLB Statcast (Baseball Savant). Displayed here as an estimate.

aliases: Batting Average on Balls In Play
entries.definition: Batting average on balls in play: how often balls put in play become hits, indexed to whether a line is running hot or unlucky.
entries.methodology: BABIP = (H - HR) / (AB - K - HR + SF). League average sits near .300. Large gaps from a hitter's own norm often regress, so it is read as a luck and contact-quality signal rather than a skill on its own; some hitters sustain higher BABIP through speed or hard contact.
entries.origin: Standard sabermetric rate; the DIPS insight that pitchers have limited control over BABIP is due to Voros McCracken.

entries.definition: Vertical approach angle: the steepness of a pitch's descent as it crosses the plate; VAAoe is that angle over expectation given the pitch's release and velocity.
entries.methodology: VAA is the angle of the ball's path at the plate. Flatter approach angles on four-seam fastballs at the top of the zone tend to generate more swing-and-miss, so VAA and VAAoe (over expectation, adjusting for release height and velocity) are read as shape context for a fastball, not a stand-alone grade.
entries.origin: Derived here from Statcast pitch tracking (Baseball Savant); the approach-angle family was popularized across the public pitching-analysis community.

entries.definition: Bond-math for a farm system: whether its prospects arrive while the big-league core is still under team control. Negative means the farm lands inside the window (aligned); positive means help comes after the core has leaked to free agency.
entries.methodology: Two pieces. System Duration (etaMean) is the surplus-weighted average arrival season of a farm: each prospect's projected ETA weighted by his expected surplus dollars, so the number leans toward the prospects who matter most. The core center (coreCenter) is the WAR-weighted midpoint of the org's controlled-core production over 2027-2031. Window Alignment = etaMean minus coreCenter. At or below zero, the farm reinforces the core while it is still cheap and productive; well above zero, the core has aged out or left before the farm shows up. The arrival curve (etaByYear) shows the share of farm surplus landing each season.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Surplus value weighed against its downside. A prospect is an option on future WAR, so upside swings are not risk; only the chance of falling short is. Higher Sortino means more expected surplus per unit of downside.
entries.methodology: Built from the same eFV surplus distribution the trade board already carries (a five-point fan from p10 to p90 plus the mean). Downside deviation is the semi-deviation below the mean (only shortfalls count). Sortino = (mean surplus minus the p10 floor) divided by that downside deviation, so a bunched, high-floor profile scores higher than a boom-or-bust one at the same mean. The tooltip also carries a risk-adjusted surplus (mean minus half the downside deviation, a local display haircut that does not re-rank the board) and the bust probability. Descriptive: it re-expresses the validated surplus model, it does not change any shown surplus.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: A market-structure overlay on a prospect's consensus FV history: candlesticks plus trader-style indicators (momentum, an RSI gauge on grade changes, realized volatility). Descriptive signals on scouting consensus, not predictions.
entries.methodology: Each candle covers one consensus snapshot: the open is the prior grade, the close is the current consensus FV, and the wick spans the range of source grades that period. Momentum is the net grade change over the last three intervals. The RSI gauge measures the balance of upgrades to downgrades over recent GRADE CHANGES only (flat re-confirmations are dropped, so a static grade never pins the gauge); above 70 reads overbought, below 30 oversold. Volatility is the standard deviation across sources on the latest grade. These are read as market context, not a forecast; the candles need at least four snapshots and the RSI at least six grade changes, otherwise the relevant piece is hidden.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Candlestick and RSI conventions are borrowed from financial technical analysis.

entries.definition: A live draft-night board: each pick as it happens, priced against our board and the historical value of that pick slot, so you see the reach or the steal in surplus dollars.
entries.methodology: During the draft a poller reads the MLB Stats API every minute and writes a read-only feed the page renders. Each pick joins to our board by name and carries the consensus FV, the reach-or-steal gap (how many spots earlier or later than our board rank the player went; a faller past his rank is a steal for the drafting team), the expected first-six-year WAR for that slot from the realized pick-value curve, and the slot surplus in dollars, plus the signing bonus against the slot value. It is a live view over already-published models, not a new projection; before the draft the board is empty.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Pick data from the MLB Stats API.

entries.definition: An options-desk view of a prospect's value. Delta is the dollars gained from a one-grade upgrade, Vega is the dollar swing implied by scouting disagreement, and Theta is the surplus lost per year of arrival delay.
entries.methodology: All three read off the same value framework the surplus board uses. Delta is the change in expected surplus dollars when the grade moves up one full grade (5 FV points), measured on the FV-to-surplus curve at the prospect's grade, so a jump near the steep part of the curve is worth more. Vega multiplies the local slope of that curve by the spread of source grades, giving the dollar value at stake in the scouting disagreement. Theta applies the framework's annual discount to the expected surplus, the value that erodes for each extra year before the prospect arrives. Implied volatility is just that grade spread. Descriptive: it re-expresses the validated surplus model as option sensitivities, it does not change any dollar figure.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. The Greeks framing is borrowed from options pricing.

entries.definition: The probability a prospect becomes a star, defined as posting two or more seasons of four or more WAR during his team-control years. Hitters run higher than pitchers, since a bullpen outcome rarely clears four WAR.
entries.methodology: The displayed figure is the FanGraphs 2026 published tier value for the player's FV and role, read straight from the published valuation set, so what you see on the board matches the published table exactly. Star is defined as two or more seasons of four or more WAR across the player's team-control years. Our own mixture model also computes a per-player version from the outcome-bucket distribution: for each bucket it draws a per-season WAR profile, sums the chance of clearing four WAR in two or more control seasons, and weights the buckets by the odds of each outcome given the grade, blending starter and reliever paths for pitchers. That model version runs below the published tiers under the current bust-heavy WAR anchors, so it is shown as a diagnostic and is being calibrated toward the published tiers rather than replacing them.
entries.origin: Published star-odds tiers from FanGraphs 2026; the per-player mixture model is Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: The share of a prospect's grade value that comes from the chance of UPGRADING to a better grade before graduating, rather than from the most likely outcome at today's grade. A grade is a call option on development: a low FV is worth more than its modal result because it can still improve before it graduates.
entries.methodology: The grade is modeled as a role-split absorbing Markov chain over FV tiers 35 to 70 plus graduated and out, with an annual step estimated from our dated grade history (FanGraphs and MLB Pipeline pooled to one grade per player per year, Laplace-smoothed); graduation is a real MLB debut and out is a washed-out player, and a still-active player's last observed year is censored so no transition is fabricated. total is the expected payoff under the full chain (the grade can move), intrinsic is the payoff if the grade were frozen at today's value, option is total minus intrinsic, and PLUS% is option divided by total. Payoff is the clemens_2026 table value of the grade a player graduates from. Low tiers are option-rich (a 45 FV hitter runs about 60 percent); high grades run low or NEGATIVE because grade mobility at the top is net-downgrade risk the frozen view ignores and the top-tier samples are thin. Provisional and descriptive: negatives are shown honestly and it does not change any surplus.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Expected slugging: the slugging percentage a hitter's batted-ball contact deserved, based on how the ball was struck, stripping out defense and park luck.
entries.methodology: Baseball Savant estimates SLG from exit velocity and launch angle using the run values of each batted-ball outcome. It answers what a hitter's contact was worth rather than what fell in for extra bases. Shown on MLB player cards as a percentile against the qualified-hitter pool for the season.
entries.origin: Baseball Savant (MLB Statcast), Tom Tango and the Statcast team; our card value is a percentile reconstruction from the tracking inputs available.

entries.definition: Expected isolated power: deserved extra-base power, computed as xSLG minus xBA, so it isolates the power a hitter's contact earned from the singles.
entries.methodology: xISO = xSLG - xBA, both from Baseball Savant's contact-quality model (exit velocity + launch angle). It is the deserved-power analog of ISO (SLG - AVG), reading through defense and park luck. Shown on MLB player cards as a percentile against the qualified-hitter pool; pairs with the Luck tile (actual wOBA minus xwOBA).
entries.origin: Baseball Savant (MLB Statcast), Tom Tango and the Statcast team; our card value is a percentile reconstruction from the tracking inputs available.

entries.definition: A reliever's DESERVED run prevention on the REM+ scale: the 100-anchored REM+ convention applied to Savant expected wOBA allowed instead of FIP, so it reflects the contact quality a reliever gives up rather than how the balls happened to fall. Luck is actual minus expected wOBA allowed. A companion to REM+, not a replacement.
entries.methodology: xREM+ = 100 times the pool-average expected wOBA allowed over the reliever's own expected wOBA allowed (INVERTED, so a lower allowed xwOBA scores higher), anchored over the reliever board so 100 is the average reliever. Expected wOBA is built from the launch conditions of each batted ball allowed, so it strips the balls-in-play and sequencing luck in actual results. HONEST FRAMING: Statcast expected wOBA allowed was tested against FIP for the pitcher run-prevention models and did NOT forward-predict better, so REM+ stays FIP-based; xREM+ is a companion contact-quality-inclusive DESERVED read plus a luck residual, never a claim of sharper prediction. Companion for tracked relievers only (Statcast is MLB-only and needs a real sample, 80+ batters faced). Luck greater than zero means the reliever allowed more than his contact deserved (unlucky, room to improve); less than zero means he over-performed (due to regress).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: A starter's DESERVED run prevention on the SEM+ scale: the 100-anchored SEM+ convention applied to Savant expected wOBA allowed instead of FIP, so it reflects the contact quality a starter gives up rather than how the balls happened to fall. Luck is actual minus expected wOBA allowed. A companion to SEM+, not a replacement.
entries.methodology: xSEM+ = 100 times the pool-average expected wOBA allowed over the starter's own expected wOBA allowed (INVERTED, so a lower allowed xwOBA scores higher), anchored over the starter board so 100 is the average starter. Expected wOBA is built from the launch conditions of each batted ball allowed, so it strips the balls-in-play and sequencing luck in actual results. HONEST FRAMING: Statcast expected wOBA allowed was tested against FIP for the pitcher run-prevention models and did NOT forward-predict better, so SEM+ stays FIP-based; xSEM+ is a companion contact-quality-inclusive DESERVED read plus a luck residual, never a claim of sharper prediction. Companion for tracked starters only (Statcast is MLB-only and needs a real sample, 150+ batters faced). Luck greater than zero means the starter allowed more than his contact deserved (unlucky, room to improve); less than zero means he over-performed (due to regress).
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Expected-stat inputs from Baseball Savant (Statcast).

entries.definition: An organization's international-amateur spending efficiency: bonus dollars committed per projected FV point, over the graded (tracked) signees in a class. Lower is more efficient. It is a PROJECTED-FV spending proxy, not realized value, because recent J2 classes have no outcomes yet.
entries.methodology: Per org, over the graded (tracked) signees only: numerator = sum of signing bonuses on those signees (covered dollars), denominator = sum of their current projected FV points (raw FV, matching the fv_per_m_pool / surplus_per_fv_pt family, no floor subtracted); $/FV pt = covered dollars / FV points. Only tracked signees carry a projected FV, so the ratio is computed over that covered subset and the Coverage column discloses the graded subset's share of the org's total class spending. Orgs with fewer than 3 graded signees in view are held out (listed, not ranked) because a one or two signee ratio is noise. This is descriptive and PROJECTED: it reads how efficiently an org converted bonus dollars into scouted grade, NOT realized MLB value, since recent classes have not resolved. Provisional; it changes no surplus number.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. IFA signing bonuses from Spotrac.

entries.definition: A roster-decision exposure read for the trade board: whether a player is Rule 5 must-protect, on the 40-man, and out of option years. It flags players an org may be forced to move or protect, which shapes trade leverage. Descriptive and deterministic, not a predictive model.
entries.methodology: Built from the player's roster status: on_40_man, option years used and left (3 to start), Rule 5 exposure (not on the 40-man and at least the exposure-year threshold since signing, so protect-by-November or lose for about $100k), and service phase. The 0-100 Crunch score is a simple additive: +55 Rule 5 must-protect or in the November urgency window, +30 on the 40-man and out of options (waiver-exposed to option), +12 one option left, +10 for occupying a scarce 40-man slot. The per-org Crunch summary counts must-protect and out-of-options players among that org's rostered / MLB board players only, which is disclosed as NOT a full 40-man census. Descriptive: there is no outcome to backtest, so no predictive gate; the inputs are exact roster facts, not a forecast.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Roster status from the MLB Stats API.

entries.definition: The average Leverage Index of the situations a player was involved in -- how high-stakes his plate appearances (batters) or entries (relievers) were on average. 1.0 is a neutral spot; above 1.0 means he saw more pressure than average.
entries.methodology: Leverage Index (Tom Tango, The Book) measures how much a single play can swing win probability relative to an average situation; pLI averages that index over all the plays a player was in. For batters we average the LI across every plate appearance from the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed. It contextualizes WPA: a high WPA at a high pLI is expected, while a high WPA at a low pLI is genuine clutch. Descriptive, not predictive.
entries.origin: Industry metric; average Leverage Index faced (Tom Tango, The Book), computed here from the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed.

entries.definition: How much better (or worse) a player performed in high-leverage spots than his own overall rate would predict. Positive means he added more win probability when it mattered than a context-neutral version of himself would have; it is a timing measure, not a skill.
entries.methodology: FanGraphs Clutch = WPA/pLI - WPA/LI. WPA/pLI is the player's win-probability added rescaled by his average leverage faced (what a context-neutral player at his rate would add), and WPA/LI is his actual context-neutral production; the difference isolates whether his value clustered in high-leverage spots. Computed here from the MLB StatsAPI winProbability feed. Descriptive and famously unstable year to year -- a realized timing read, not a projection.
entries.origin: Industry metric (FanGraphs), from the win-expectancy framework (Tom Tango). Clutch = WPA/pLI - WPA/LI.

entries.definition: S-XLINE is the Statcast measurement upgrade inside eFV: for AAA seasons from 2023 on, a prospect's stat line is blended toward what his contact quality says it should have been before eFV converts it into level-relative features. The idea is simple: two hitters with the same batting line are not the same hitter if one earned it with 92 mph contact and the other ran a lucky BABIP. Expected stats built from exit velocity and launch angle measure the skill under the results, and they predict the NEXT season better than the results themselves. S-XLINE feeds eFV that better measurement. Players without a qualified Statcast season are untouched.
entries.methodology: Derivation: for each AAA season since 2023 with at least 100 Savant plate appearances, S-XLINE takes the gap between the player's expected and actual stats measured within Baseball Savant (xBA minus BA, xOBP minus OBP, xSLG minus SLG for hitters; the xwOBA-against gap for pitchers) and applies half of that gap as a correction to the stat line eFV reads. Measuring the gap within one source cancels any cross-source level bias. Validation, run before shipping: on 776 AAA hitter season pairs the blended line predicted next-season wOBA better than the actual line (delta Spearman +0.025, CI95 +0.005 to +0.045); on 491 pitcher pairs the contact-quality blend cleared at +0.051 (CI95 +0.012 to +0.091). Safety bounds: per-stat gaps are capped (25 points of BA or OBP, 50 points of SLG, applied at half weight) and the pitcher ERA correction is clamped to plus or minus 25 percent, so a single hot or cold partial season can never move a served grade more than 3 FV points; the shipped run moved 97 active grades, largest move 2.7. The gate record lives in the model registry (xfv_statcast_line). Coverage note: public MiLB Statcast exists where tracking hardware is installed, currently AAA parks; if MLB extends tracking to AA the blend extends automatically.
entries.formula: Hitters: adjusted stat = actual + 0.5 x capped(x_stat - stat). adjusted OPS = adjusted OBP + adjusted SLG. Caps: 0.050 for BA and OBP, 0.100 for SLG. Pitchers: adjusted ERA = ERA x clamp(1 + 0.5 x (xwOBAa - wOBAa) / wOBAa, 0.75 to 1.25). Applies only to AAA seasons 2023+ with 100+ Savant PA.
entries.example: A AAA hitter slugs .556 but his exit velocity and launch angle support only .357. Without S-XLINE, eFV prices the inflated line. With it, roughly half of the capped gap comes off before the level-relative features are built, and his grade settles about 2 FV points lower, closer to what the underlying contact quality has actually earned.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Descriptive ladder-speed index for hitters: how fast a prospect has climbed the affiliated minors versus peers on a comparable path. 100 = typical pace, 110 = one standard unit faster, display capped 70-130. Hitters only, and never an input to any model.
entries.methodology: Raw pace is area pace: PA-weighted average ladder height (Complex 1 up to Triple-A 5) per active season, counting only meaningful assignments (30+ PA at a level-season) and freezing at the MLB debut. Expected pace comes from a joint fixed-effects fit over starting-level x experience cells plus entry age, era, position group, and entry pathway, so every cohort margin centers near 100. AP+ = 100 + 10 x the standardized residual, shrunk toward 100 for thin samples; the percentile compares hitters with the same number of active seasons. Sample tiers: Insufficient (score suppressed), Early, Developing, Established. The cancelled 2020 season never counts as development time, and the score is descriptive display only: by the source method's own contract it feeds no eFV, projection, valuation, or ranking surface.
entries.formula: AP+ = 100 + 10 x z, where z = (area pace - peer expected pace) / experience-year SD, shrunk by m/(m+1) on m meaningful assignments; display capped 70-130.
entries.origin: Will Cahoon's Advancement Pace method (descriptive display charter), rebuilt for eephus.io from the platform's own MiLB season data by Noah J. Dengler.

entries.definition: Card chip for premium-position prospects (listed C, SS, CF, 2B, 3B): the modeled probability the player's primary MLB home stays at his listed position, banded Likely stays / Split risk / Likely moves. Risk context only - never part of any grade, rank, or sort.
entries.methodology: Stay probability comes from the platform's position-migration defense model: the listed position mapped through established migration base rates (roughly 47 percent of shortstops stay at short, 94 percent of catchers stay behind the plate), with body frame (BMI) and age pushing probability mass down the defensive spectrum. Bands are tercile cuts of stay probability among tracked prospects at the SAME listed position, so a catcher is judged against catchers, and the cut points ship with the data and appear in the chip tooltip. The chip reads base rates plus frame, not scouting reports, and it changes no served number anywhere on the site.
entries.origin: Position-migration thesis by Will Cahoon; chip banding built for eephus.io by Noah J. Dengler.

entries.definition: Per-pitch-type pitch-quality display on CollegeSavant pitcher pages, scored from TrackMan physics (velocity, movement, release, spin) for NCAA arms. Its own class-relative ratio scale (100 = college-average expected run value, 0 = the worst observed college xRV), NOT a z-score index: the measured payload spread is about 23 to 24 points per season with observed values from 3.4 to 185.4. Descriptive context for draft evaluation, not a projection.
entries.origin: Industry metric. External model lineage built by Will Cahoon for CollegeSavant (college TrackMan xRV family); eephus.io vendors the already-scored payloads and displays them, and does not fit or re-derive the model. Registered for governance 2026-07-23 (data/collegesavant_stuff_eval.json).

entries.definition: Card pill for A-ball and complex-level prospects: the player's whiff share (hitters) or four-seam velocity (pitchers), and the part of that signal his own strikeout rate does not already explain. Display context. It is not a grade, not a projection, and it applies no adjustment of its own.
entries.methodology:
Coverage is the tracked bake in data/statcast_alevel_signals.json: 635 player-seasons whose current level is A or CPX with at least 100 pitches of signal exposure (330 A hitters, 144 complex hitters, 96 A pitchers, 65 complex pitchers), 2026 only. A player outside that set has no pill.

Each signal is z-scored inside its own side-level-season qualified pool, then regressed on the same player's current strikeout z with coefficients FROZEN on the 2023-2025 lab populations and never refit at serve time: hitters whiff_z on k_z, slope 0.887, intercept 0.014, r 0.872, n 788; pitchers velo_z on k_a_z, slope 0.218, intercept -0.009, r 0.219, n 227. The pill reads the RESIDUAL, so a positive hitter residual is swing-and-miss the strikeout rate has not charged for yet, and a positive pitcher residual is velocity the strikeout rate has not converted yet.

What the residual is worth was measured, once, as an incremental Spearman against the out-of-fold residual of a cross-fitted stat-line ridge: whiff on next-season K% +0.0965, CI95 [+0.0277, +0.1604]; FB velo on next-season K%-allowed +0.1423, CI95 [+0.0196, +0.2704] (data/xfv_statcast_line4_eval.json). The same pass read NULL on the hitter wOBA channel, -0.0266 with a CI95 that crosses zero. So the whiff residual is STRIKEOUT information and nothing wider; read it as bat-to-ball risk, not as a general hitting verdict.

Limits worth holding onto: one live season, no resolved out-of-sample fold, and a forward correlation rather than a backtest against realized WAR. Registered provisional (model_id statcast_alevel_display). Whether the same residual also leans the served eFV grade is a separate registered decision (model_id xfv_statcast_overlay_uncapped), not something this pill does.
entries.formula: residual_z = signal_z - (slope x strikeout_z + intercept), coefficients frozen 2026-07-23; hitters signal = whiff share, pitchers signal = four-seam velocity.
entries.example: A Single-A hitter at 35.2% whiff sits at whiff_z +1.17 with a K% z of +1.08, so his residual is +0.20: the contact problem is about what his strikeout rate already says. The same whiff share on a hitter striking out at pool average reads +1.15, and that gap is the case the pill exists to surface.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. The inputs are MLB Statcast and zone tracking; the residualization against the stat line and its frozen coefficients are ours.

entries.definition: Historical strata a prospect falls into (age for level, level, level-relative production and so on) with what those groups actually realized. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. The predictive version of this object was tested and failed, so nothing here corrects, adjusts or forecasts a grade.
entries.methodology:
Population: hitters with a MiLB track record and a decision year of 2016-2024, 904 rows. Every WAR and bust number is computed on the 527 whose six-year window has actually closed, which in practice means decision years 2016-2020. Baseline is 1.90 mean WAR and a 76.7% bust rate at or below 0.5 WAR; a stratum is only interesting against that baseline. A stratum is one to three axis cuts intersected, and 3,957 clear the reporting floor of 25 complete-window players. Each reports n, mean and median realized WAR, a 95% interval on the mean, and the bust rate. Read that as a description of who has been in the box, not as a forecast for the player standing in it. Hitters only; there is no pitcher table. 130 strata carry a zero-width interval because every closed member realized the same WAR (in practice 0.0, none reached the majors): that is a degenerate interval, not a precise one.

Why it is not a model. Nested cross-validation put stratum selection inside the fold, and the effect did not survive it. On the hitter side every arm's rank-correlation delta against the shipped eFV blend is inside its own null band (-0.0106 to +0.0082, no interval clean of zero) against the 0.017 the gate standard sets. Between 45 and 141 percent of the in-fold selected effect is selection bias: inner-fold effects of 0.86 to 1.85 WAR collapse to -0.60 to +0.50 out of fold, and the row-permuted zero-information control arms invert outright. Selection is unstable on top of that, with eight nested folds picking eight different top strata (mean pairwise axis Jaccard 0.135).

What is and is not auditable. Stratum MEMBERSHIP is reproducible and is re-checked on every build: all 3,957 ids and resolved-row counts match the pre-registered outcome-blind enumeration exactly. The outcome columns are not. The script that produced them (tools/_comb_sweep_desc.py) is absent from the tree and nothing else writes that file, so mean WAR, median WAR, bust rate and the residual t are carried as a frozen quote of a 2026-07-25 measurement rather than a statistic anyone can regenerate. The strata are honest; the numbers attached to them are unverifiable.

The reliability tag. The source artifact's own health_warning claims every stratum has a statistically zero out-of-fold residual against the shipped eFV model. That is FALSE and it is not carried forward: 477 of 3,957 strata sit at |t| >= 2 where about 180 are expected under a true null, 124 at |t| >= 3 against about 11 expected, max 4.91. Each stratum instead ships a tag from its own t. PRICED (3,193) means the comps and the grade agree. WATCH (687) means nominally off-model but not surviving Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.05 across all 3,957 tests, so it is unverified rather than a finding. OFF-MODEL (77) survives that correction at |t| >= 3.30 and means the comps and the grade DISAGREE, with neither authoritative. Read the off-model tier carefully: 76 of the 77 carry a negative residual and 43 busted at a 100 percent rate, because WAR floors near zero for a player who never debuts, so any positive expectation on a young low-grade group is guaranteed a one-sided residual there. That is the outcome scale bottoming out, not a correctable eFV defect. Registered unvalidated with no eval artifact (model_id archetype_comps); the failed model lane is registered separately as archetype_search.
entries.example: The stratum 'very young for level, above-average level-relative OPS' shows 26 closed-window players, mean 11.7 WAR, CI95 [8.6, 14.9]. That is what those 26 did. It is not a projection for the 27th, and no eFV grade moves because of it.
entries.origin: Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. Built from the 2026-07-25 combinatorial archetype sweep (tools/_comb_sweep.py family) and registered as a descriptive surface rather than a model.

entries.term: MiLB Park Factor (Run PF / HR PF)
entries.definition: In-house run and home-run park factors for 201 minor league venues, 2021 forward. 1.00 is neutral for that venue's league and season; 1.10 means the park played about 10% more runs than its league-season baseline. The displayed number is a trailing three-season window and it is not clamped. Reference context only: no grade, rank or dollar on this site is park-adjusted.
entries.methodology:
Team-season factor = (home runs scored plus allowed per game) / (road runs scored plus allowed per game), from StatsAPI final scores, regular season only. Each team-season is centered on the unweighted league-season mean ratio, then shrunk toward 1.00 empirical-Bayes style with K_G = 70 home games, so a short or lopsided schedule pulls back to neutral instead of reading as a park. A venue takes its modal home team; a venue-season is the home-game-weighted mean of the team-seasons played there; the three-season window uses only seasons at or before the season being read, so a historical row never sees its own future.

Coverage: 1,211 team-seasons from Triple-A down through the rookie complexes and the Dominican Summer League, 969 venue-seasons, HR factor on 930 of them. 2026 is in season, so its numbers mix a partial schedule with the 2024-2025 window legs.

Why the WINDOW and not the season. Single-season factors are not stable enough to publish: venue-level year-over-year Spearman on the run factor runs 0.353 to 0.479 across the five season pairs, under the 0.50 bar the park registration set. An independent split-half of the multi-season aggregate (2021/2023/2025 against 2022/2024/2026, no shared season) reads 0.735 on runs and 0.760 on HR. So the trailing window ships and the single season does not.

Why it is NOT clamped. The source method block carries application clamps of [0.90, 1.10] run and [0.80, 1.25] HR. Those are a safety rail for a frozen model formula, not a statement about a ballpark, and that model path is switched off. Clamping the display would move 13 venues on runs and 17 on HR and would turn Hodgetown's measured 1.209 into 1.100, so the measured value ships and the bounds travel alongside as context. Two other honest omissions: HR factor feeds no formula anywhere (ISO and SLG neutralize through the run factor), and StatsAPI venue 401 'TBD' is excluded from the table because it is the unlabeled-DSL bucket, not a ballpark, and pools 133 team-seasons against itself so its factor is 1.00 by construction.

Model status, stated plainly: the eFV lane that would have park-neutralized MiLB stat lines with this table FAILED its registered gate (hitters +0.0005 with lo95 -0.0011, pitchers -0.0021 with lo95 -0.0051) and stays gated OFF. The table is real and face-valid; the correction built on it was measured and did not earn a ship. Registry rows: milb_park_factors (the table and its display surface) and xfv_park_line (the failed correction).
entries.formula: run_pf = shrink( (home RS+RA per game) / (road RS+RA per game) / league-season mean, K_G = 70 ); venue-season = home-game-weighted mean over its team-seasons.
entries.example: Hodgetown in Amarillo reads 1.209 run / 1.428 HR and Dickey-Stephens Park in North Little Rock reads 0.840 run / 0.751 HR. Both are Double-A. The same raw slash line means different things in those two boxes, which is the entire use of the table.
entries.origin: Park factor is a shared industry concept; this table is an in-house build from StatsAPI schedule scores by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io. No external park-factor source is used.

entries.definition: Every source's published FV is quantile-mapped onto one common scale before it is averaged, and the result is rounded UP. That is why the consensus can sit above or below the arithmetic mean of the grades printed on the card. The per-source grades shown are always the raw published ones.
entries.methodology:
Three steps sit between the grades on the card and the consensus number.

1. NORMALIZE. Each source's grade distribution is quantile-mapped onto the FanGraphs scale using only the players both graded, per role per cycle, so a source that only covers the top of the board is not called hot for skipping the low tiers. A source that grades hot maps DOWN and a source that grades cold maps UP. Direction is measured per cycle, never assumed: the 2026 hitter cycle maps MLB Pipeline and ESPN down by a median 5 FV against FanGraphs and Pipeline International down by 10, while Just Baseball and tjstats map flat. The reference source maps to itself.

2. AVERAGE. The normalized grades are averaged. Weighting is EQUAL as of 2026-07-25: accuracy weights shipped in 2026-06 and were reverted when the hardened re-measurement put the weighted arm inside the noise floor. A player only one source has ever graded is pulled one third toward FV 35 until a second grade lands.

3. DISPLAY. The result is clamped to 20-80 and rounded UP to a whole grade, the site-wide rule for FV and tool grades. A raw 50.05 prints 51.

So the printed grades are not the inputs and their average is not the output. The gap is mapping first, the single-source pull second, and the round-up rule last, and the round-up alone is worth up to a full grade. Registered as model_id grade_normalization (provisional, data/grade_normalization_eval.json); the map is refit each cycle and recomputation is deterministic.
entries.formula: consensus FV = ceil( mean( map_source(published FV) ) ), clamped 20-80; single-source case shrunk = (n_obs x src_FV + k x 35) / (n_obs + k).
entries.example: Three sources print 45, 50 and 50 and a reader averages 48.3. The model never sees those three numbers. It sees each grade after its own scale map, averages those, and prints the ceiling: a mapped mean of 50.05 displays as 51. Nothing about the card's per-source column changes.

entries.definition: The model behind /arbitration/. It estimates the one-year salary an arbitration-eligible player receives for a season in which his club tenders him a contract and the figure is settled or awarded through arbitration.
entries.methodology: Two stages, because a first trip and a later trip are different problems. The first arbitration year has no prior arbitration salary to raise from, so it is a level model on log deflated salary, fit by ridge on projectable features only - WAR, playing time, age, position, service class and the Arkmetric skill indices - with a Duan smearing correction so the served figure is a conditional mean rather than a median. Second and later years are a raise problem, and the collective agreement caps a cut at 20% of the prior salary, so the target is transformed rather than clamped: the model predicts the log of the raise above that floor, which makes every prediction and every band endpoint legal by construction. On measurement the per-player model did not beat a simple empirical raise multiplier for those later years, so the board serves the multiplier there and the model only where it earned its place. Only seasons whose arbitration year comes from published service time are scored. Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.

entries.definition: Actual arbitration salary minus what this model expected. It asks whether the arbitration system paid a player more or less than players with a comparable case.
entries.methodology: This is the model's own residual, so it sums to roughly zero across the league by construction, and a negative value means the model expected a higher salary than the player received. It is a statement about the model, not a verdict that a player is underpaid. It is deliberately kept separate from the value residual, which compares salary to on-field production priced at that winter's dollars per win and does not sum to zero, because arbitration systematically pays below the open market. Averaging a quantity centred on zero with one that is not centred on zero produces neither of them, so the two are never combined anywhere on the surface. Arkmetric, created by Noah J. Dengler, original to eephus.io.
